body: You can start a game three ways: from the game list in the left sidebar, from the game grid on the start screen, or straight from this wiki via the pre-game screen.
Before every game the pre-game screen appears: pick the mode there (e.g. single or multiplayer) and reach the options and this wiki.
If a game has many modes or the window is small, Options, Wiki and Back move into a single row on the pre-game screen - so everything stays visible.
- [Esc] pauses and resumes the running game - in menus it goes back.
- [F11] toggles fullscreen on and off.
- The green Back to menu button ends the game and saves the high score - so does switching to another game from the sidebar.
On the left you see all games with their icon and your high score (star). The running game stays highlighted; on small windows the list scrolls with the mouse wheel.
The status card at the bottom left shows the game name, state (green = running, gold = paused, red = game over), score and the current frame rate.

20 games have a local 2-player mode: Snake, Pong, Air Hockey, Tic-Tac-Toe, Tetris (Versus), Asteroids (co-op duel), Memory, Connect Four, Tank Duel, Reversi, Yahtzee, Draughts, Chess, Nine Men's Morris, Simon, Billiards, Minigolf, Pinball, Bowling and Battleship - selectable on the pre-game screen.
In single player both key bindings control the same character; in multiplayer one each (default: P1 = WASD, P2 = arrows or IJKL - see options).
Tetris also offers Versus against the AI; in two-player Battleship a handover screen hides the fleets. The web version is single-player only.
Toggle sound and set the volume in the options screen. All effects are generated live - there are no audio files.
Haptics vibrates a connected gamepad (does nothing without one).
Three presets are available: WASD + arrows, WASD + IJKL and arrows + WASD.
Every single key can be rebound: click a row or confirm with Enter, then press the desired key. [Esc] cancels.
Bindings are separate for player 1 and player 2 and are saved permanently.

Five actions per player can be rebound: up, down, left, right and action. Some games add fixed keys on top - such as hold [C] and rotate left [Z] in Tetris, or undo [U] in 2048, Chess and Sudoku. They only work if that key isn't bound to an action; the game's setup hint and wiki page list them.
The resolution sets the internal play area (480x360 up to 1280x960). Smaller = less load, bigger = sharper image.
Auto-resolution adapts the play area to the window size automatically.
The FPS options (15 to 120) set the target frame rate - fewer FPS saves power.

The Appearance tab lets you pick one of ten UI designs: UI v4.2 (default: Midnight Glass - a deep midnight gradient with slowly drifting glows in indigo, turquoise and magenta, fine film grain and frosted-glass panels), UI v4.1 (subtle stars plus Saturn and a black hole), the four pattern variants UI v4.1.1 to v4.1.4 (like v4.1, but with a tiled zigzag pattern as the background - black/charcoal, blue/dark blue, v4's indigo on black and v4's graphite tone on black), UI v4 (a calm, flat graphite look), UI v3 (the classic UI with aurora lights and glow), UI v2 (the very first UI rework: navy gradient, starfield and glowing buttons, no animations at all) and UI v1 (the look before the UI rework: plain background, flat buttons, no effects).
Every card shows a small preview. The choice applies instantly to the game area and the sidebar and is stored in settings.json.

The interface is available in 14 languages: German, English, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Polish, Turkish, Danish, Norwegian, Swedish, Finnish, Czech, Slovenian and Croatian. Switch in the options screen or via Language in the sidebar - this wiki switches language too.
Every game saves its best value automatically when a round ends. A new record shows a golden banner - plus confetti rain.
You can see the best values everywhere: as a star in the sidebar list, in the ticker on the start screen and in the status card.
Modes without a high score - such as Sprint and Ultra in Tetris, the Crossy Road daily route or 2048 with undo - show no banner; the game keeps their best times and daily bests itself.
- settings.json: sound, volume, key bindings, resolution, FPS, design and game options (e.g. Snake mode, Tetris DAS/ARR, Sudoku variant, Battleship rules).
- mem.json: high scores, the chosen language, achievements and statistics - plus the progress of many games in their own sections (see below).
- mem-ngb.json: Snake's visual mods (head color, grid, banner).
- replay.json: the saved replays of Minigolf and Bowling.
- ugc.json: your own Minigolf holes and Geometry Dash levels (shared as .lamapgzmap or .lamapgzlevel).
These files live right in the game folder and can simply be deleted to reset.
Every game with progress has its own section in mem.json, for example:
- sudoku: solved levels with stars and best times, puzzles in progress and the Daily Sudoku with its streak.

- casino: the Llama Bank account - the llama chips for Blackjack, Poker, Casino, Lama Crossing, Lama Mines, Lama Plinko and Lama Crash with each game's balance, plus a Lama Crossing round, a Lama Mines round and a Lama Crash flight in progress, the Lama Mines auto marks and the history, fairness data, statistics and carried-over fractions of Lama Mines, Lama Plinko and Lama Crash.
- crossy: collected coins, bought characters and the Crossy Road daily best.
- tetris: best Sprint time, best Ultra score and the Versus record against the AI.
- g2048: saved 2048 games and best scores per board size and mode.
- chess: your progress in Chess puzzle mode.
- geodash: best percentage per level (Normal and Practice), coins found, attempts and jumps in Geometry Dash.
- wordle: statistics per mode, language and word length, the state of the daily word and the best scores.
Plus minigolf, pinball, bowling, lamatowerdef and others with their best results.
mem.json and settings.json are written crash-safe: first to a temporary file, then swapped in a single step. The previous version stays behind as mem.json.bak or settings.json.bak.
If mem.json is ever damaged, the game automatically reads the backup - so high scores, achievements and llama chips are not lost.

Points are saved when a round ends, when you leave via Back to menu, when you pick another game from the sidebar mid-game or when you quit the collection. Only a crash or a hard kill of the program loses the round in progress.
Several players on one device: every profile has its own high scores, achievements, level, statistics, llama chips and saved games.
The Profiles button in the sidebar lists them all; the card above it shows who is playing, with level and XP bar.
Only the device settings (resolution, sound, key bindings, theme) and the interface language are shared.
Up to eight profiles are possible.
New profile: type a name, pick an icon and a colour, save. The name goes through the word filter and may be 14 characters long.
Click Play (or press Enter) to switch - from then on every point, minute and achievement goes to that profile.
Keys on the screen: Enter switches, N creates, F2 renames, Del deletes, Esc goes back.
Deleting a profile deletes its data too; the last profile always stays.
When you start a multiplayer mode, the collection first asks which profile plays as player 2 - or you play as a guest.
In game the profile names appear instead of Player 1/2.
Every multiplayer match goes into the head-to-head record: the Profiles tab of the progress screen shows who beat whom how often.
It also holds the device leaderboard: which profile holds the best score in each game.
All profiles live in mem.json under players/<id>; the statistics are in stats.pgzlamastats. Both sit next to the game (or next to the .exe).
On the first start after the update your existing save moves into profile 1 - nothing is lost.
Replays and self-made courses stay available to everyone, but carry the name of the profile that recorded or built them.
The collection keeps track: playtime, rounds, wins, records, days played, score curves and every unlocked achievement - with a timestamp.
It all lives behind the Achievements & statistics button in the sidebar, spread over five tabs (Tab or click switches).
Only active playtime counts; pauses and menus do not. Every profile has its own statistics.
- Achievements: everything by category, with rarity, points, date or a progress bar. Level, rank and XP bar sit on top; a filter shows only open or unlocked ones.
- Statistics: summary cards, the ten most played games as bars, a ring for wins/losses and the table of all games.
- Calendar: the days-played map (the darker, the longer), current and best streak, weekdays and time of day.
- History: everything with a timestamp - achievements, records, level-ups, duels - plus one game's score curve as a line.
- Profiles: every profile with level and playtime, the device leaderboard and the head-to-head record.
Above the calendar sits your PyGameZ recap: best day, favourite time, longest session in one go, favourite game and your rarest achievement.
All charts react to the mouse: hover and a small box names the date, playtime and rounds.
Records are marked as golden dots in the score curve.
All statistics live in the file stats.pgzlamastats next to the game - ordinary JSON, one block per profile.
On the calendar tab (or with E and I) you can export and re-import it; the web version reads the same file.
On import you choose whether the values are added to the current profile.
So the file cannot grow forever, history (4000 entries), score curves (250 per game) and calendar (about three years) are capped; the totals stay.

Six games record their rounds: Minigolf, Bowling, Billiards, Pinball, Snake and Tetris. What is stored is the actual motion - frame by frame, thirty times a second. The replay therefore looks exactly like your round, HUD and scorecard included.

Minigolf, Bowling, Billiards and Pinball have short sequences (stroke, roll, shot, ball). Snake and Tetris run on - there a sequence is a ten-second part; Snake is always shown from above, even if you played in 3D.
Only the current round is recorded. Start a new one and the recording starts over as well.
If the round was a good one, press [P] on the round-end screen - the replay starts right away. [S] puts it into the archive, [E] shares it as a file, [Esc] returns to the round-end screen.
The Billiards practice mode never ends: there [P] shows what happened so far between two shots, and the frame carries on afterwards.
Unsaved recordings are gone with the next round; the archive holds 20 replays per game.
The Replays button in the sidebar opens the archive: one tab per game, with result, date and running time of every recording.
- [Enter] plays, [Del] deletes (press twice), [Tab] switches the game.
- During playback [Space] pauses, Left/Right jumps to the next sequence, Up/Down changes the speed (0.5x to 4x).
A click on the progress bar jumps to any position.

[E] writes the recording as a .lamapgzreplay file - from the archive as well as right after the round. It holds exactly one replay and can be passed on like a minigolf course or a Geometry Dash level.
[I] reads such a file back in. It lands in the tab of the matching game and carries a small arrow there - the sign that it came from somewhere else.
A recording that is already in the archive is not imported twice.
On the first start and in the options under Recording you can turn Record replays off - then nothing is captured at all.
Very long games are trimmed after roughly half an hour; the bar then shows Recording trimmed.
The recordings live in replay.json in the game folder, sorted by game. You may delete that file at any time.
Every game remembers its matches. In the pre-game screen, the Matches button opens the game's history.
- Last matches: a curve of the last 30 results (records in gold) and below it the last 10 matches.
- All matches: every saved match, with a mode filter [M] and newest/best sorting [O].
At the top you see the totals: matches, wins, best, average and play time.
Date and time, mode, points (chip games: profit or loss), win/loss/draw, duration and details such as bet, multiplier, coins, level or opponent.
- Records are marked in gold. If you leave a round early, it shows as aborted - but only if you already had points or it ran for at least 5 seconds.
- Chip games count every round separately, Geometry Dash every level visit, Labyrinth every solved level.
The last 250 matches per game are kept (on pygamez.com 50 by default). Older ones drop out - the totals still keep counting.
The history lives in matches.pgzlamamatches next to mem.json, separately for each profile.
274 achievements across all 50 games - from your first start to a Perfect Clear in Tetris.
Every achievement has a rarity and therefore a point value; the sum is your level.
Find them behind the Achievements & statistics button, tab Achievements. A filter hides open or unlocked ones.
- General: collection-wide goals - rounds, games tried, playtime, records, wins, days played, daily streaks, level and duels. Plus extras like night owl, marathon or weekend player.
- Score milestones: a fair target score for each game.
- Master tiers: the second, much higher mark - only for games whose score is open-ended.
- Regular: 25 rounds of one game. Exists for each of the 50 games.
- Special moments: checkmate, a Yahtzee, the 4096 tile, a hole-in-one, an air hockey hat-trick, four ghosts on one power pill and much more.
Five tiers, five point values: common 10, rare 25, epic 60, legendary 150, mythic 300.
The colour shows in the badge, in the stripe left of the row and in the pop-up when it unlocks.
Legendary and mythic achievements celebrate with confetti.
The top right of the tab shows how many of each tier you already have.
Achievement points make your level: level 2 costs 20 points, each further level 8 more than the one before.
Every few levels the rank changes - from Llama Chick through Point Hunter and Master Llama to Star Llama (14 ranks).
Level and rank appear in the sidebar, in the header of the achievements tab and, on every level-up, as its own pop-up with a fanfare.
On the first start after the update your existing achievements count right away - a card shows your starting level.
Unlocked achievements live in mem.json with their profile; points, level and the history are in stats.pgzlamastats.
Every profile collects for itself - switch and you see your own achievements.
In 2048 and chess, rounds with undo or hints count neither for the high score nor for achievements.

Endless mode with level climbing: you start with exactly one apple. The more apples you collect in total, the higher your level - more apples appear at once and the score multiplier rises (15 levels, up to x16).
- Blue apples open a slot machine: the stake is your length, three equal symbols = jackpot with bonus apples.
- Purple apples (gambling) bet part of your size: normally a 50 percent stake with a factor of x0.5 to x1.5.
Your exact size is shown as a decimal in the top left - every bet builds on it. The level tiers live in games/levels/snake-comp.json and are freely editable.
Toggle with [H] in the competitive setup: every boost eats length, and purple apples get riskier (75 to 90 percent stake, factor x0.25 to x2.25). A red border marks the mode.
Reachable with [P] in single player: collected apples can be converted into prestige levels that grant lasting perks. Progress persists across runs.
In the setup via the brush button or [C] : a pure looks menu that never changes gameplay.
- Head: the snake's head color (presets or a custom RGB color).
- Grid: a coordinate grid with row numbers and column letters as a guide on big boards.
- Banner: toggle the multiplier banner, plus size and opacity - with live preview.
Everything is stored in mem-ngb.json.
With [V] in the setup: the board is rendered as a 3D scene, a chase camera floats behind the snake and steering is relative to the view direction (two quick presses = U-turn).
With [K] you open the 3D camera options: smooth shake, field of view (FOV), camera height and the turn-shake toggle. Playable in 3D: Classic and Obstacles (single player only).
Steer with [W] [A] [S] [D] or the arrow keys. In 3D you steer relative to the view direction: left/right turn, two quick presses = U-turn.
- Boost: hold [Space] or Shift = double speed. The stamina bar drains and recharges afterwards.
- Player 2 boosts with Enter or the right Shift key.
- Classic: pure snake.
- Speed rush: every food makes you faster.
- Obstacles: deadly blocks on the board.
- Portals: teleporter pairs move you across the board.
- Time attack: 60 seconds, as many apples as possible.
- Competitive: endless mode with levels, slot machine and gamble apples - details on the Snake special page.
Also selectable: wall wrap, bonus apples, hardcore, 2D/3D view with [V] and multiplayer.
Apples give points (bonus apples randomly double). Gold apples appear temporarily, give lots of points and refill the boost instantly. In competitive your level multiplies all points.
- Use the boost on long straights, not in tight corners.
- With wrap enabled you can escape over the edge when you box yourself in.
- In competitive, purple apples pay off best when you have spare length to stake.
Player 1 moves the left paddle with [W] and [S] - in multiplayer, player 2 controls the right one with the arrow keys.
The movement mode is switchable per control: continuous (press once, paddle keeps going) or hold (moves only while pressed). Toggle with [X] for control 1 and [N] for control 2.
Play to 5 points, against the AI or with two players.
The ball physics accelerate with every hit; the bounce angle depends on where the ball meets the paddle.
- Hit the ball with the paddle edge to create steep angles.
- Hold mode gives finer control, continuous mode faster reactions.
In single player your mallet follows the mouse - any key switches back to keyboard control (8 directions).
In multiplayer P1 plays left with [W] [A] [S] [D] and P2 right with [I] [J] [K] [L] .
- AI difficulty: easy, medium or hard.
- [T] picks the goals to win (3/5/7/10).
- [P] toggles power-ups: XL (bigger mallet), GOAL (opponent's goal shrinks), speed (faster mallet). Power-ups belong to the player who touched the puck last.
- The puck inherits your mallet speed - build momentum instead of just blocking.
- Stay behind the puck: pushing it towards your own goal risks own goals.
Place marks with a mouse click. After the game ends: Enter or click = new round, [S] = back to the settings.
Board sizes from 3x3 up to 9x9. The winning length adapts: 3 in a row on 3x3, 4 on 4x4, otherwise 5.
Single player against the AI (easy/medium/hard) or two players locally, X versus O in turns.
- The hard AI on 3x3 is unbeatable - a draw is the best you can get there.
- On big boards the center matters most: most 5-lines pass through it.
Move the paddle with the mouse or arrow keys. [Space] launches the ball and fires the laser. [P] or [Esc] pauses.
- [1] [2] [3] picks the difficulty.
- Left/right changes the ball color, up/down the start level, [M] the layout (standard or full).
Brick types: normal, steel (indestructible), bomb (explodes) and gold (extra points).
Power-ups: x2/x3 balls, [L] laser, [F] fireball, [G] sticky, [U] shield, coins for bonus points - plus a combo multiplier for fast hits.
- Play the ball along the side walls behind the brick block - it clears by itself up there.
- The shield catches exactly one breakthrough: save it for risky multiball phases.
Solo: pick the variant in the setup. Marathon is endless and the level rises every 10 lines (start level 1-15) - only Marathon counts for the high score.
- Sprint 40: clear 40 lines as fast as you can; your best time is saved.
- Ultra 2:00: score as many points as possible in two minutes; your best score is saved.
Versus AI: play against an AI with three strengths (Easy, Medium, Hard). Clearing lines sends garbage to the other side; whoever tops out first is K.O. Your record against each strength is saved.
2 Players (PC version only): the same for two people on one keyboard. Both fields always get the same piece sequence.

[Left] [Right] move the piece - hold them and it starts sliding after the DAS, then keeps going at the ARR rate. [Up] rotates right, [Down] is the soft drop, and the action key (default: [Space] ) drops the piece instantly (hard drop).
- [C] or [Shift] puts the piece into hold (once per piece), [Z] or [Y] rotates left, [X] rotates right.
- 2 Players: player 1 holds with [Q] and rotates left with [E], player 2 holds with right [Shift] and rotates left with right [Ctrl].
- These fixed keys only work if you haven't assigned them to an action yourself.
In Sprint and Ultra, [R] restarts instantly. After a game: [R] = play again, [S] = setup - the hard drop keys deliberately don't restart anything.
In the setup you adjust DAS (delay before auto-shift), ARR (speed after that, 0 ms = straight to the wall) and the ghost piece.
Pieces come in a 7-bag: each of the seven pieces appears exactly once per group of seven. The preview shows the next 5.
Rotation follows SRS: if a piece is blocked, the game tries up to four alternative positions (wall kicks) - so pieces can even be spun around edges.
On the ground a piece waits 0.5 seconds before it locks. Every move or rotation resets that time, at most 15 times per depth.
Game over: the new piece has no room, a piece locks entirely above the playfield, or garbage pushes the stack out of the top.
All values times level: Single 100 · Double 300 · Triple 500 · Tetris 800.
T-Spin: no lines 400 · Single 800 · Double 1200 · Triple 1600. T-Spin Mini: 100 · 200 · 400.
- Back-to-Back: a Tetris or T-Spin right after another one counts x1.5.
- Combo: every further line clear in a row adds 50 x combo x level.
- Perfect Clear (empty playfield): +800 / 1200 / 1800 / 2000, as a Back-to-Back Tetris +3200.
- Soft drop gives 1 point, hard drop 2 points per row.
A T-Spin counts when the T piece locks after a rotation and at least three of the four corners around its center are filled (walls and floor count too).

If both corners on the side its nose points to are filled, it's a full T-Spin, otherwise a Mini. If the T rotates into the gap with the big kick (one column sideways, two rows down), it always counts as full - that's how the T-Spin Triple works.
Callouts above the field show T-SPIN, TETRIS, BACK-TO-BACK, COMBO and PERFECT CLEAR.
Attack: Double 1 · Triple 2 · Tetris 4 · T-Spin Single 2 · T-Spin Double 4 · T-Spin Triple 6 · Mini Double 1. Plus +1 for Back-to-Back, +1 to +5 for long combos and +10 for a Perfect Clear.

Incoming garbage appears in the warning bar left of the field: yellow means it's still waiting, red means it rises with your next piece that clears no lines - at most 8 rows per piece, each batch sharing one hole.
When you clear lines yourself, your attack first cancels the waiting garbage; only the rest goes to your opponent.
Every 40 seconds the pieces fall faster (up to level 12).
- Build flat and keep one edge column free for the I - four lines at once bring points and attack.
- Use hold to save an I for a Tetris or to park a piece that doesn't fit.
- In Versus, Back-to-Back pays off: two Tetrises in a row send 4 + 5 lines.
- Achievements: Tetris! (4 lines at once), Spin to Win (T-Spin Double), Squeaky Clean (Perfect Clear), Sprinter (Sprint 40 under 2:00). There are no achievements in 2-player mode.
- Classic: the classic alien block descends. In the setup you choose movement (left/right only or free with WASD) and aiming (always up or at the mouse).
- Arena: free movement in all directions, enemies stream in from all edges, you aim in your movement direction.
Four weapons, switch with [1] to [4] : blaster, spread shot, rapid fire and laser.
Destroyed aliens drop power-ups: extra life, shield and weapon upgrades. Every 4th level has a boss.
- The spread shot clears dense blocks, the laser pierces whole columns - switch per wave.
- Never stand still in the arena: circle along the edge and pull enemies into a line.
Up thrusts in the view direction, left/right rotates the ship, the action key fires. The ship keeps drifting (inertia) and wraps around the screen edges.
Down triggers hyperspace: an emergency jump to a random position with a 4 second cooldown - and a 12 percent risk of breaking apart.
Rocks split into two smaller ones; the three sizes give 20/50/100 points. The UFO (can be disabled) gives 200 points, an extra life comes every 5000 points.
Power-ups from destroyed rocks: shield (6 seconds invulnerable), triple shot and rapid fire.
Co-op duel (multiplayer): both ships fly at once with separate lives - whoever has more points wins.
- Clear the small, fast splinters first before you crack the next big rock.
- Hyperspace is a last resort, not a travel option - the risk is real.
Move with the arrow keys or [W] [A] [S] [D] . After the game ends: Enter = new, [S] = setup.
The tunnels on the left and right warp you to the other side.
The four ghosts hunt with their original behaviors: Blinky chases directly, Pinky sets up ambushes, Inky uses a vector via Blinky, Clyde backs off up close.
Power pellets make ghosts blue and edible for a while - the chain gives 200/400/800/1600 points. Fruit appears as a bonus, an extra life comes at 10,000 points.
Difficulty normal/hard/extreme sets ghost speed and frightened time; every level gets faster.
- Eat a power pellet only when several ghosts are close - the chain is what counts.
- Remember the scatter phases: at every switch all ghosts turn around.
[Space], arrow up, [W] or a mouse click makes the bird flap - it tilts with its climb and sink speed.
Every pipe passed gives one point. Coins (bonus) and a shield power-up that forgives exactly one collision appear in the gaps.
Day and night themes change with the score; after the game over there are medals from bronze to platinum.
- Short, regular taps keep the flight path calmer than rare long ones.
- The difficulty sets gap size and speed - the gap narrows as your score grows.
The doodler jumps automatically on landing - you only steer left/right (with inertia). The edges are open: leaving left brings you back in on the right.
Shoot upwards with arrow up or [Space] .
- Green: normal. Blue: moves. Brown: breaks when stepped on. White: vanishes after one jump.
- Springs give a super jump, the propeller hat carries you up automatically for a moment (invulnerable).
- Monsters are deadly on contact - shooting them gives extra points.
Score = height reached; difficulty rises with height.
- Plan where to land before jumping off - brown platforms won't carry you.
- Use the open edge as a shortcut to far-away platforms.
Arrows or [W] [A] [S] [D] slide all tiles in one direction at once. With a mouse or touchpad you can also swipe: press, drag in the direction you want, release.
Held keys don't repeat - every move is its own key press. Input during an animation is remembered and carried out right after.
[U] or [Backspace] = undo, [R] or [N] = new game, [Tab] = back to the setup. These extra keys only work if you haven't assigned them to an action yourself.
Equal numbers that collide merge into their sum. Each tile merges at most once per move: 2, 2, 4, 4 slid left becomes 4, 8.
After every valid move a new tile appears - usually a 2, one time in ten a 4. When no move is possible, the game is over.
From 4096 on, tiles get their own colours from green through blue and violet to crimson (131072); even bigger tiles are dark with golden digits.
Board size from 3x3 to 8x8 - small boards are tricky, big ones leave lots of room for long chains.
- Classic: the goal is 2048. Then the game asks whether you want to keep playing - [Enter] continues, [N] starts a new game.
- Time attack: 3 minutes, as many points as possible. The clock starts with your first move; the bar below the board shows the time left.
- Endless: no goal and no interruptions until no move is left.
Choose in the setup: off, 3 per game or unlimited. Undo takes back the last move including its points - even right after game over.
Once you use it, the game counts as played "with undo": it counts neither for the highscore nor for the tile achievements, and its best score is kept separately.
The running game is saved automatically for each size and mode - after your moves and when you leave the game.
The setup then offers Resume with the points and moves of the saved game. New game discards that save.
Every merge scores the value of the new tile. The info column shows score, best, moves, biggest tile, undos left and time.
Best scores and the biggest tile are stored per size and mode. The 2048 highscore only counts in 4x4 Classic without undo.
- 2048!: create the 2048 tile.
- 4096!: create the 4096 tile.
Both count on boards up to 4x4 and only without undo - in any mode.
- Park your biggest tile in a corner and never disturb that corner.
- Slide mainly in two directions - it keeps the board sorted.
- In time attack speed matters: merge early and keep your tiles together in one corner.
Left click reveals a cell, right click places a flag (optionally with a question-mark cycle, [Q] in the setup). [F] flags the cell under the cursor, [R] restarts.
Chording: clicking a satisfied number (all flags placed) reveals the remaining neighbors at once.
Beginner (9x9, 10 mines), intermediate (16x16, 40) and expert (30x16, 99). The best time per level is saved.
The first click is always safe - mines are placed only afterwards. Points = level base value minus seconds.
- Start with the numbers at the edge of open areas - the patterns there are unambiguous.
- A 1 in a corner with only one covered neighbor is always a safe flag.
In the setup you pick the variant at the top and the difficulty below it. Every variant has 4 difficulties times 100 fixed levels, each uniquely solvable.
- Classic: the familiar 9x9. The 400 levels are the same as before the update - ticked-off levels stay ticked off.
- X-Sudoku: both diagonals also contain every digit exactly once (subtly marked).
- Killer: hardly any givens, but dashed cages instead. The digits of a cage add up to the small sum in its corner and never repeat. Easy has small cages and more givens, Expert has big cages.
- Mini 6x6: 2x3 boxes and only the digits 1 to 6, with extra-large cells.

- Daily Sudoku ([T] or the card on the right): one classic puzzle per day, the same for everyone - in the browser too. The difficulty depends on the weekday (Monday easy, Tuesday and Wednesday normal, Thursday, Friday and Sunday hard, Saturday expert). Solve it every day to build a streak.
Select a cell with the arrow keys, [W] [A] [S] [D] or a mouse click. The number pad on the right works entirely with the mouse and shows under each digit how many are still missing.
- [1] to [9] enters a digit, [0], Delete or right click erases.
- [U] or [Z] undoes, [Y] redoes.
- [N] toggles notes, [C] fills in all candidates automatically, [H] gives a hint.
- [M] tints the cell with a color marker ("Color markers" switch in the setup).
- [R] restarts the puzzle, [Q] opens the level select, [A] shows the solution after the game ends.
"Digit first" input (setup, key [I]): pick a digit first, then click as many cells as you like or place it with Space.
In the setup: [1] to [4] difficulty, [V] variant, [T] daily sudoku, [F] error limit, arrows + Enter start a level. The letter keys only work if they are not assigned to an action in the options.
The game mode sets the assists and the score multiplier:
- Classic x2.0: no assists, pure like on paper.
- Notes x1.5: plus pencil notes and automatic candidates.
- Comfort x1.0: errors red instantly, conflicts and wrong cage sums highlighted, correct entries lock in.
- Assist x0.7: additionally up to 3 hints.
Every entry is checked against the solution immediately. With the 3-error limit the third mistake ends the game - undo does not erase a mistake.
Points = (base of variant and difficulty minus time, errors and hints) times the multiplier. All variants and the daily sudoku count for the high score.
Every level awards up to 3 stars: 1 for solving, 2 without mistakes and hints, 3 additionally under the target time of the difficulty (shown in the level info).
The level select shows stars, best time and solved levels; a dog-ear marks puzzles in progress.
Puzzles in progress are saved automatically - when leaving, when returning to the level select and regularly while playing - and resume next time. If you switch modes, the lower multiplier counts.
Achievements: "Cage Fighter" for your first Killer Sudoku, "Star Collector" for 30 levels with 3 stars.
The daily puzzles of the last 30 days and every day you have already solved are in the daily archive - with best time and stars per day.
- Below the daily card, the arrows or [Page up]/[Page down] change the day, [K] or Archive opens the calendar, [T] starts the chosen day.
- Archive puzzles don't change your daily streak.
- Start with rows, columns and boxes that already hold many digits.
- Note candidates in pairs: if two cells of a unit share the same two candidates, those drop out everywhere else in the unit.
- Killer: every row, column and box adds up to 45. If cages lie almost entirely inside, the rest gives away the remaining cell.
- Killer: some sums have only one combination - 3 in two cells is always 1+2, 17 is always 8+9.
- X-Sudoku: the diagonals are two extra units - check them early, the first digit often hides there.
Hop cell by cell with the arrow keys or [W] [A] [S] [D] .
- [R] restarts, [S] opens the setup.
After the game over: [Enter] = retry.
At the bottom 5 traffic lanes with cars and trucks in alternating directions - contact is deadly.
Above, 5 river lanes: logs and turtles carry you; falling into the water means drowning. Turtles dive periodically on higher levels (blinking = warning).
At the top wait 5 bays - filling all of them completes the level, then everything speeds up.
- Extras: a bonus fly (+200) appears briefly in empty bays, crocodiles occupy bays on higher levels (landing = death), and the time bar at the bottom drains per frog.
Every newly reached row gives 10 points, a bay 50 plus 10 per remaining second.
All 5 bays award 1000 points and the next level.
At 10,000 points you get a one-time extra life (start: 3 lives).
- Plan traffic gaps one lane ahead instead of waiting at the edge.
- Use logs drifting towards your target bay as a taxi.
- Land early: the time bonus beats a detour to the fly.
Flip cards with a mouse click - or move the frame with arrows/WASD and flip with [Space] or [Enter] .
- [R] shuffles a new round, [S] opens the setup.
A mismatched pair stays visible briefly and then flips back by itself.
Three board sizes: 4x4 (8 pairs), 6x6 (18) and 8x6 (24) - the motifs are shape-color combinations.
Solo, every revealed two-card combination counts as a move; the clock is running.
- Duel (multiplayer on the pre-game screen): take turns flipping, a match means you go again - whoever has more pairs at the end wins.
Solo: board-size base minus 15 per move and 2 per second (minimum 100).
Duel: the winner's pairs times 100 go to the high-score list.
- Flip unknown cards first - each one shows you a motif for free.
- Anchor motifs by their color group, it halves the search space.
- In a duel never reveal a fresh pair for your opponent.
Drag cards with the mouse (drag & drop) or move them click-by-click; right click sends the top card to the foundation (Klondike/FreeCell).
- [U] undoes any number of moves, [R] deals a new hand, [S] opens the setup.
[Space] or [Enter] operates the stock (draw/deal).
- Klondike: the classic solitaire - four foundations from ace to king, tableau descending in alternating colors; option: draw 1 or 3.
- Spider: 10 columns, 104 cards - complete king-to-ace runs of one suit vanish; option: 1, 2 or 4 suits.
- FreeCell: everything face up, 4 free cells; supermoves are limited by free cells and empty columns.
- Pyramid: remove pairs summing to 13, the king counts alone; 2 redeals.
- TriPeaks: always one rank above or below the waste pile (ace and king wrap) - long chains give combo points.
Klondike: +10 per foundation card, +5 per revealed card, time bonus on winning. FreeCell: +10 per foundation card plus time bonus.
Spider: 500 minus moves plus 100 per completed run. Pyramid: +5 per card, +500 for clearing.
TriPeaks: 10 times combo per card - the stock resets the combo; +500 for clearing.
Draw-3 (Klondike) and the Spider suit count are saved permanently.
Undo is unlimited and free - feel free to experiment.
All variants share one high-score list.
- Free aces and twos as early as possible (Klondike/FreeCell).
- Keep one column empty - it is your most important tool (Spider/FreeCell).
- In Pyramid, count the reachable 13-pairs before touching the stock.

The mouse steers the camera directly like in a shooter: every movement turns the view instantly by that amount (the cursor is captured invisibly inside the window). [Esc] pauses and releases the mouse. Yaw is unlimited, up/down clamps at 60 degrees.
Left click shoots exactly through the screen center (short cooldown between shots).
- [+] and [-] change the sensitivity (even mid-game), [E] ends a chill session.
- Precision (60 s): always 3 orbs at once - shooting one spawns a new one instantly; an accuracy bonus is added at the end.
- Reflex (30 targets): targets appear one at a time and shrink away after a moment - reaction time counts, stats at the end.
- Moving targets (60 s): orbs drift on paths (swinging, orbiting, bobbing) - consecutive hits raise the combo multiplier.
- Chill (endless): no timer, no miss penalty - just relax and shoot; the score is saved when you return to the menu.
Precision: 100 points per hit plus a distance bonus; at the end accuracy squared times 1500 on top.
Reflex: the faster the reaction, the more points (1000 minus milliseconds, at least 50).
Moving targets: 80 points times the combo multiplier (up to x4 at 12 consecutive hits) - a miss resets the combo.
Chill: 50 points times the multiplier; the combo only fades after 5 seconds without a hit.
- Space (default): a full star sphere, a black hole with a brightly glowing ring and a distant planet.
- Neon: a synthwave arena with a glowing floor grid and a striped sun.
- Range: an indoor hall with lanes, lamps and classic bullseye targets. Theme and adjustable motion blur (0 to 80 percent, key [B] or setup buttons) are saved.
- Small, calm mouse movements hit better than frantic swipes - the view follows 1:1.
- Low sensitivity for precision, higher for reflex and moving targets.
- Distant targets have a small forgiveness margin - hold steady instead of overcorrecting.
Two colours take turns dropping discs into one of 7 columns; each disc falls to the lowest free cell. The first to line up four - horizontally, vertically or diagonally - wins the round.
In single player you face the AI (three strengths in the setup); in 2-player mode you take turns at one mouse or keyboard.
The starting player alternates every round. [Enter] starts the next round, [S] returns to the setup.
- Mouse: hover over a column (the preview disc shows the spot) and click.
- Keyboard: [Left] [Right] pick the column, drop with [Down], [Space] or [Enter].
- Direct pick: the numbers [1] to [7] drop straight into that column.
Easy deliberately misses some threats and sometimes plays only the second-best move - great for learning. Medium plans a few moves ahead and blocks reliably.
Hard searches much deeper and punishes every mistake instantly - only double threats win here.
Every win against the AI scores one point; the highscore is the most wins in one session. There is no scoring in 2-player mode.
- The centre column is the strongest: most four-in-a-rows run through it.
- Build double threats (two open threes at once) - your opponent can only block one of them.
1-versus-1 in an arena of walls: hit your opponent to take the round - first to 5 rounds wins the match.
Shots bounce off walls once (ricochet) and vanish on the second contact. Careful: a bounced shot can hit you too.
Play against the AI (three strengths) or with two players on one keyboard. After the match: [Enter] = rematch, [S] = setup.
- Player 1: [W] [S] drive forward and back, [A] [D] turn, [Space] fires.
- Player 2: arrow keys drive and turn, [Enter] fires. The bindings follow the options.
- At most 4 of your shots live at once, with a short reload in between.
- Rapid fire: 8 seconds with almost no reload.
- Shield: absorbs exactly one hit (ring around the tank).
- Triple shot: the next 5 shots fan out in three directions. Power-ups appear every few seconds in the arena and expire after 12 seconds.
Four arenas to choose from: Open (no cover), Cross, Pillars and Maze - or Random, which rotates the arena every round.
The easy AI drives around aimlessly and aims poorly; the medium one chases you and sidesteps.
The hard AI keeps its distance, leads its shots ahead of your movement and even banks shots off walls on purpose.
Against the AI you score per match win: more for higher strengths and clean victories; points add up across rematches. There is no scoring in 2-player mode.
- Use the walls: banking shots around corners hits without exposing yourself.
Goal: get closer to 21 than the dealer without going over. Number cards count face value, pictures 10, the ace 11 or 1.
The game uses a 4-deck shoe; the dealer draws to 16 and stands on every 17.
Place your bet first (chip buttons or keys [1] to [4], [Backspace] clears it), then deal with [Enter].
- Hit [H]: draw another card.
- Stand [S]: keep your current total.
- Double [D]: double the bet, take exactly one card, then stand automatically - only on your first two cards.
- Split [X]: separate two equal-value cards into two hands (once per round; split aces get just one card each).
- Blackjack (ace + ten-value card) pays 3:2.
- A normal win pays 1:1, a push (tie) returns your bet.
- Bust or lose: the bet is gone. If the dealer shows an ace or a 10, they immediately check for blackjack.
Blackjack, Poker, Casino, Lama Crossing, Lama Mines, Lama Plinko and Lama Crash share one account at the Llama Bank: you start with 1000 llama chips and your balance is saved permanently.
Your bet is taken as soon as the cards are dealt - leaving a hand in progress loses it.
The highscore is the peak of your blackjack balance: 1000 plus everything you have won and lost at blackjack. Wins at roulette, the slot or poker don't count here.
Below 10 chips you are broke: [Enter] takes a bank loan and fills your account back up to 1000. Loans don't count towards the balance.
- Basic strategy: against an upcard of 7 or higher draw to 17; against 4 to 6 stand early - the dealer often busts there.
- Always split aces and eights, never split tens.
You fly through a curving neon tube, dodging bars, blocks and ring gates - one hit and the run is over.
Golden coins float in the gaps; they score extra points and usually mark the safe line.
Ring gates have exactly one hole: thread through it instead of dodging.
- Endless: the speed keeps rising and the gaps get tighter - how far can you get? A crash ends the run and saves the highscore.
- Levels: 30 fixed tracks with a finish line, from relaxed to brutal. Completed levels get ticked off; session points add up.
- Keys (default): [W] [A] [S] [D] or the arrows push the ship around the tube.
- Mouse: toggle in the setup with [C] - direct 1:1 steering, the cursor is captured and [Esc] releases it.
- [B] cycles motion blur in 10-percent steps (0 to 80, saved).
- In level mode: [R] retries after a crash, [S] opens the selection.
- Endless: 10 points per metre plus 50 per coin.
- Levels: 1000 for the finish, 50 per coin and a time bonus when you beat the par time.
The level-mode highscore is your best session total - playing several levels in a row pays off.
- Watch the rings far ahead: the tube telegraphs its curve early enough to countersteer.
- Stay near the centre when possible - every gap is reachable from there.
50 seed-generated mazes that grow with every level. Find the green pulsing exit - it always sits at the point farthest from the start.
Blue orbs float around the maze; every collected orb earns bonus points.
Completed levels get ticked off in the selection; [Enter] at the finish starts the next one right away.
- First person (3D): Wolfenstein-style view with mouselook - right in the middle instead of above.
- Top-down (2D): the classic map from above, with no mouse capture at all. Toggle in the setup with [V]; the choice is saved.
- First person: [W] [S] forward and back, [A] [D] strafe, the mouse turns your view - or turn with [Q] and [E] on the keyboard.
- [M] toggles the minimap, [Esc] pauses and releases the mouse.
- Top-down: [W] [A] [S] [D] or the arrows walk in world directions.
- Reaching the exit: 500 points.
- Per orb: 100 extra points.
- Plus a time bonus when you beat the level's par time; session points add up to the highscore.
- Right-hand rule: always following the same wall is guaranteed to reach the exit.
- The orbs roughly line the way to the exit - collecting them usually means you are on track.

Reversi (Othello) is played on an 8x8 board. You place a disc so that one or more of the opponent's discs are trapped in a straight line between the new disc and another disc of your colour - horizontally, vertically or diagonally. All trapped discs flip to your colour.
A move is only legal if it flips at least one disc. If you have no legal move, your turn is passed automatically. When neither player can move, the game ends and whoever has more discs wins.
In single player you (Black) face the AI; in two-player mode Black and White alternate.
- Mouse: click an empty square. Legal squares are marked with a small dot.
- Keyboard: the arrow keys (or your movement keys) move the selection frame, [Space] or [Enter] places the disc.
- After a round: [Enter] = new round, [S] = back to setup (single player only).
Easy plays mostly at random, Medium looks a few moves ahead, Hard searches deeper and values the corners highly.
- Corners are golden: a disc in a corner can never be flipped again.
- Beware the squares next to a corner - they often hand the corner to your opponent.
- Having fewer discs but more mobility in the midgame is often better than having many.
Every win against the AI is worth one point; the high score is the most wins in a session. Two-player games are not scored.
You have 5 dice and up to 3 rolls per turn. After each roll you may keep any dice and reroll only the rest. Then you record the result in exactly one of the 13 categories.
Each category can be used only once. If nothing fits, you cross one out for 0 points. After 13 turns the sheet is full and the game is over.
Single player is a high-score chase for the highest total; in two-player mode you fill two sheets in turns - the higher total wins.
Upper section (Ones to Sixes): counts the pips of that number. If your upper section totals at least 63, you earn a 35-point bonus.
- Three/Four of a kind: sum of all dice if at least 3 resp. 4 are the same.
- Full house = 25 (three plus a pair), Small straight = 30 (four in a row), Large straight = 40 (five in a row), Yahtzee = 50 (five of a kind), Chance = sum of all dice (always allowed).
- [Space] or the Roll button rerolls the dice that are not held.
- Click a die or press [1] to [5] to hold or release that die.
- Click a category or pick it with the arrow keys and press [Enter] to score it.
- After the game: [Enter] restarts.
- Grab the 63-point upper bonus early - fives and sixes are especially valuable.
- Use Chance to rescue a bad roll; cross out Yahtzee or a straight if nothing works out.
Guess the hidden word. After each guess the tiles change colour: green = right letter in the right spot, yellow = the letter appears but somewhere else, grey = the letter is not in the word.
Repeated letters are handled correctly: a letter is only marked yellow or green as often as it actually occurs in the answer.

Every guess has to be a real word - it is checked against the word list of the selected language and length (4,000 to 19,000 accepted guesses, depending on language and length). Anything else is rejected: the row shakes briefly and the guess does not count. The answers are always common words of the same language - no names and nothing offensive.
Endless: one word after another with 6 guesses each. The first word you fail to crack ends the game.

Daily word: one word a day with 6 guesses - the same for everyone in each language and length, on the PC and in the browser. A daily word you have started is saved; afterwards the game shows your result, statistics and the countdown to the next word. Your streak only grows if you play every day.
Dordle: two words at once in 7 guesses - every guess counts for both boards. The keys of the on-screen keyboard are split: left half board 1, right half board 2.
Quordle: four words at once in 9 guesses. The keys are split into quarters and show the colours of all four boards.
The daily words of the last 30 days and every day you have already played can be replayed - per language and word length.
- In the daily word setup, the arrows or [Page up]/[Page down] change the day, [K] or Archive opens the calendar.
- Archive words don't count for statistics and streak; started archive words are saved.
Before each game the setup screen appears - next to it you see your statistics for the selected mode and length.
- Word length: 4, 5, 6 or 7 letters, each length with its own word lists.
- Hard mode: revealed hints must be reused - green letters stay in place, yellow ones have to appear again. In Dordle and Quordle a guess has to fit the hints of at least one unsolved board.
- Colour-blind mode: orange instead of green and blue instead of yellow - in the shared result too.
All settings are saved right away.
- Type letters A-Z, [Backspace] deletes the last one, [Enter] checks the row.

- You can also use the on-screen keyboard with the mouse: QWERTZ for German, Czech, Slovenian and Croatian, AZERTY for French, QWERTY otherwise. Its keys colour in based on what you have learned so far.
- The slider icon in the top right corner takes you back to the setup.
- In the setup: [4] to [7] or [Left] / [Right] = word length, [H] = hard mode, [F] = colour-blind mode, [Enter] = start.
- After a game: [Enter] = play again, [C] = share result, [S] = setup. [Space] hides the result so you can look at the boards.
Endless: each solved word scores points - fewer guesses means more (10 to 60). Only Endless with 5 letters counts for the high score; the other lengths keep their own best scores.
Statistics are kept per language, length and mode: games played, win rate, current and best streak and the guess distribution as a bar chart - the bar of your latest solve lights up.
[C] or the Share button copies your result to the clipboard as an emoji grid - without giving away the answer - so you can paste it into any chat. A * after the score means hard mode.
- Mind Reader: guess a word in 2 tries or fewer.
- Word Habit: solve 7 daily words in a row.
- Quad Genius: solve all four words in Quordle.
- Open with a word that has many different, common letters.
- Use grey letters to rule things out and move yellow letters to a new position.
- In Dordle and Quordle, first guess words that give hints for several boards at once.
Start running with [Space] or [Up] - the dino then runs automatically.
- Jump: tap [Space]/[Up] for small hops, hold for higher jumps.
- Duck: hold [Down] - in the air this makes you fall faster.
Cacti appear singly or in groups on the ground - jump over them.
Pterodactyls show up at three heights: high = duck, low/mid = jump.
Speed keeps rising; every 100 points you get a beep and a short blink.
Toggle on the start screen (saved): [1]-[3] difficulty, [N] day/night, [C] skin.
- Tapping briefly saves height for quick double obstacles.
- After a crash, continue right away with [Enter]/[Space].
Chosen in setup - each with 1 player vs AI or 2 players local:
- German Draughts 8x8: men capture forwards and backwards, the king flies any distance.
- International Draughts 10x10: bigger board, forced capture with the maximum rule (longest capture is mandatory).
- Checkers 8x8 (English): men capture forwards only, the king moves just one square.
Captures are forced: if a capture exists you must take it - capturable pieces are outlined in red.
Click a piece, then the target square; play a multi-jump step by step.
Keyboard: [Arrows]/[WASD] move the frame, [Space]/[Enter] selects.
A man reaching the far row becomes a king (crown).
Single-player offers three AI strengths (minimax + alpha-beta), pick them in setup with [<]/[>].
The high score counts your wins against the AI this session; multiplayer is not scored.
After a game: [Enter] new round, [S] back to setup.
Pick the variant in the pre-game screen:
- Texas Hold'em: against 1-3 AI opponents, with dealer button, blinds and four betting rounds (preflop, flop, turn, river).
- 5 Card Draw: heads-up vs AI - swap cards once, two betting rounds.
- Video Poker (Jacks or Better): solo against the paytable.
During betting: [F] fold, [C] check/call, [R] raise, [A] all-in - or click the buttons.
When swapping/holding: click cards or press [1]-[5], then [Enter] to draw.
[Enter]/[Space] deals the next hand.
You play with the llama chips of the Llama Bank - one account shared with Blackjack, Casino, Lama Crossing, Lama Mines, Lama Plinko and Lama Crash (start 1000, saved permanently).

At the start of a hand your account sits on the table as your stack; whatever goes into the pot is taken immediately. If you leave the table mid-hand, your share of the pot is gone - the rest goes back to your account.
The highscore is the peak of your poker balance: 1000 plus everything you have won and lost at poker. Wins in other games don't count here.
Broke (less than the big blind of 20, in Video Poker less than 10) = bank loan with a click, your account is back at 1000.
Hand ranking: High Card < Pair < Two Pair < Three of a Kind < Straight < Flush < Full House < Four of a Kind < Straight Flush < Royal Flush.
Chess with the complete rule set: every piece move, short and long castling, en passant and pawn promotion with a choice of queen, rook, bishop or knight.
A game ends in checkmate, resignation, a lost clock or a draw - by stalemate, the fifty-move rule, threefold repetition, insufficient material or agreement.
Three modes: a game against the AI, 2 players on one computer (desktop only) and puzzles.
Next to the board you see both players with clock, captured pieces and material balance (e.g. +2), and below them the move list in standard notation - scroll it with the mouse wheel.
- Mouse: click one of your pieces or drag it straight to the target square. Legal targets, the last move and a king in check are highlighted.
- Keyboard: [Arrows] or [WASD] move the selection frame, [Space] or [Enter] picks the piece and moves it.
- Castling: move the king to its target square or onto your own rook. On promotion the piece choice appears.
- Buttons: [U] or [Backspace] undo, [H] hint, [F] flip board, [O] offer a draw, [X] resign.
- After the game: [Enter] new game (colours swap), [S] setup, [P] save the game as PGN.

Six AI levels from Beginner to Master: Beginner moves at random, the middle levels deliberately vary their play, Hard and Master search with iterative deepening, a transposition table and quiescence search and know common openings. The AI thinks in small slices per frame - the game never stutters.

Clock: none, 1+0, 3+2, 5+0 or 10+5 (minutes + seconds added per move). It starts after the first move. Running out of time loses - unless the opponent can no longer checkmate at all, then it is a draw.

Chess960: one of 960 random starting positions, its number is shown above the move list. When castling, the king still lands on g or c and the rook on f or d; the squares in between must be empty and the king may not pass through check.
Undo takes back two half-moves against the AI, the hint shows the best move as a blue arrow. Both make the game "assisted": a win then does not count for high score, statistics or achievements.
Offer a draw: the AI only accepts if it considers its position equal or worse - otherwise it declines and you can only offer again a few moves later.
The high score counts your unassisted wins against the AI in this session. Beating the Master (level 6) unlocks the "Grandmaster" achievement.
After the game you can save it as a PGN file (in the browser: download and clipboard) and replay it in any chess program.
White and Black take turns on the same computer; clock and Chess960 work as against the AI. With "Turn the board after every move" in the setup the board rotates to the side to move after every move.
Offering a draw asks the opponent, resigning applies to the side to move. Two-player games are not scored, and the browser version does not offer this mode.
200 puzzles in five stages: Mate in 1, Mate in 2, Mate in 3, Tactics I and Tactics II - 40 each, from easy to hard. Solved puzzles get a tick and your progress is saved.

First the opponent plays their last move, then it is your turn. A wrong move is taken back after a short note, the opponent's reply comes automatically. In mate puzzles every move that mates immediately counts.
- [H] show the solution (the puzzle then does not count as solved), [U] retry, [N] next puzzle, [M] back to the list.
Solving 25 puzzles unlocks the "Puzzle Cracker" achievement.
Source: the puzzles come from the freely usable puzzle database of lichess.org (CC0) and were verified with our own engine - thank you, Lichess!
- Develop your pieces early, castle, and put the rooks on open files.
- In puzzles look for checks, captures and threats first.
- With a clock, don't think too long - the increment in 3+2 and 10+5 saves many endgames.
- Placing: both sides take turns placing their nine pieces on free points.
- Moving: after that a piece slides along a line to a neighbouring free point.
- Flying: whoever is down to three pieces may jump to any free point. This rule can be switched off in the setup.
You lose when you drop below three pieces or cannot move any more.

Three of your pieces on one line form a mill: you immediately remove one enemy piece. Pieces inside a closed enemy mill are off limits as long as others are available - the legal targets are highlighted.
- Mouse: click a free point. To move, pick your own piece first, then the target; possible targets light up.
- [Esc] cancels a selection you did not mean.
- After the round: [Enter] for a new round, [S] back to the setup (single player only).
Three strengths using minimax with alpha-beta pruning. It weighs material, closed mills, mobility and open double mills - differently in each phase; the easy level blunders on purpose.
The high score counts your wins against the AI in this session; multiplayer is not scored.
Tip: a double mill - two mills that open and close alternately - decides almost every game.
- Classic: repeat the sequence exactly. Every round adds one pad.
- Speed: like Classic, but the playback gets faster every round.
- Reverse: the sequence has to be entered backwards.
- Duel: two players build the sequence together - repeat everything, then add one pad. Whoever slips loses.
- Mixed: the mode changes every round between Classic, Speed and Reverse.
The number of pads - 4, 6 or 9 - sets the difficulty.
Sound is off (colours only), on (every pad has its own tone) or mixed, where some rounds play tones and others do not. The sound switch in the options takes precedence.
- Mouse: click a pad. Keyboard: the number keys [1] to [9].
- While the sequence plays back the game ignores input - wait until it is your turn.
- After a mistake: [Enter] to try again, [S] back to the setup.
The high score is the longest sequence you repeated without a mistake; the duel is not scored.
Tip: say the colours or numbers in your head. Tones make it much easier to remember - which is why the mixed setting is the hardest exercise.
- 8-ball: pot your whole group first - solids or stripes - then the black. The group is assigned on the first legal pot.
- 9-ball: always hit the lowest ball first; whoever legally pots the 9 wins.
- Practice: no rules, no opponent - pot as many balls as you can. When the table is empty it is re-racked and counting continues.
- Mouse: moves the aim, hold the left button to charge power, release to shoot.
- Keyboard: [Left] and [Right] aim, [Up] and [Down] set the power, [Space] shoots.
- After a foul the cue ball is in hand: place it on a free spot with the mouse and click.
- [V] switches the view: 2D from above, 3D as a fixed angled view, or Free - there you swing the camera around the table with the right mouse button held down. The choice is saved.
There are three AI strengths; with two players you take turns on the same computer.
The high score counts frames won against the AI, or the balls potted in practice mode.
After the game: [Enter] for a new game, [S] back to the setup.
Put the numbered tiles back in order (1, 2, 3 …); the gap stays in the bottom-right corner.
Tiles can only slide into the empty gap. Three sizes: 3×3 (easy), 4×4 (classic) and 5×5 (hard).
The board is shuffled with many random moves, so it is always solvable.
- Click a tile in the same row or column as the gap to slide the whole line.
- Arrow keys push the tile next to the gap into it.
You start with a base score per size; every move and every second subtract a little. Solving fast and with few moves gives the best high score.
After solving, Enter/click starts a fresh board right away.
The computer picks a hidden code of coloured pegs (colours may repeat). Crack it row by row.

After each guess you get feedback pegs: a BLACK peg = right colour in the right spot, a WHITE peg = right colour in the wrong spot. The order of the feedback pegs does not reveal which peg it refers to.
Modes: Easy (4 pegs, 6 colours, 12 rows), Classic (4/6, 10 rows) and Hard (5 pegs, 8 colours).
- Click a colour at the bottom (or keys 1–8) to fill the next empty slot.
- Click a placed peg to clear it; < or Backspace removes the last one.
- OK or Enter checks the full row.
Like Wordle it is an endless streak: each cracked code scores points (fewer guesses + harder mode = more), then a new code appears at once.
The first code you fail to crack ends the game - the total is your high score.
Shoot bubbles up into the honeycomb field. When three or more of the same colour touch, the group pops.
Bubbles that lose their link to the top row when a group pops fall down and give bonus points.
Modes: Easy (4 colours, no new rows), Classic (5 colours, an extra row drops in now and then) and Hard (6 colours, faster).
- The cannon aims at the mouse; left/right arrows also turn it.
- Left-click or Space shoots. Bubbles bounce off the side walls.
- The small bubble to the left of the cannon is your next colour.
Popped and dropped bubbles score points; clearing the whole field gives a bonus.
As soon as a bubble locks in below the red line the game is over - the total is your high score.
Guess the hidden word letter by letter. Each wrong letter draws another part of the hangman.
After 6 mistakes the figure is complete and the round is lost.
Modes by word length: Short words (3–5), Mixed (3–12) and Long words (7–12). Words match the selected language and use only A–Z.
- Type letters A–Z or click them on the on-screen keyboard.
- Correct letters appear in the word; wrong ones turn the key grey.
Endless streak: each guessed word scores points (more remaining lives and longer words = more), then a new word appears at once.
The first loss ends the game - the total is your high score.
A 3D Minecraft-style platformer: jump across floating block platforms to the glowing goal beacon. Every level is a fresh, seed-generated parkour and gets harder.
The camera is first-person like Minecraft by default; press V to switch to a chase camera.
Fall below the platforms and you lose a life and respawn at the last checkpoint. At 0 lives (you start with 3) the run ends.
Every block carries a real pixel texture: grass with its green overhang, dirt, stone, oak planks, the diamond block at the goal, slime blocks and wood for ladders and fences.

On top of that: the Steve figure with a walk cycle in the chase camera, the first-person hand, the beacon beam above the goal, spinning gold ingots as coins, a square sun, pixel clouds and hearts in the HUD.
Press T to change the texture detail: high, low or off. On slower machines 'low' or 'off' runs noticeably smoother; your choice is saved.
- WASD or arrow keys: move (relative to where you look). Space: jump. Mouse: look around.
- On a ladder, W climbs up and S climbs down. A spring block launches you high into the air.
- V = view (first/third person), B = motion blur, C = capture/release mouse, +/- = sensitivity. Esc pauses and frees the mouse.
- T = texture detail (high/low/off).
- Grass/dirt/stone/wood: solid blocks you jump on and stand on.
- Ladder: climb up/down slowly. Fence: a small block that blocks the path - just jump over it.
- Spring block: launches you high (to reach tall platforms). Coins float along the route for extra points.
Each coin is worth 50 points. Reaching a level's goal gives 1000 points plus a time bonus (the faster, the more).
Points accumulate across all levels; the total is your high score.
Enemies march along the path in waves. Build towers next to it to stop them before the exit - every breakthrough costs lives (bosses 5), at 0 the run ends.
Every map is endless: waves keep growing stronger and a boss arrives every 8 waves. Between waves you build at your leisure; you start the next one yourself.
Kills earn gold, plus wave bonuses and 5% interest. Locked maps unlock via your best wave.
- Click a tower card (or 1-9), then place it on the field. Right-click cancels.
- Click a tower: Upgrade [U] (up to 3 levels), Sell [X] (70% back). In Maximal mode you pick an A/B specialisation at top level.
- [Space] starts the wave, [F] = 2x speed, [G] = show all ranges, mouse wheel scrolls the build bar. Maximal: [Q] Meteor, [W] Frost Nova, [E] Gold Rush.
- Arrow = fast & cheap, Cannon = area damage, Frost = slows & reveals, Sniper = huge range, pierces armor, hits flyers.
- Classic adds Poison (damage over time), Tesla (chain lightning, anti-air) and Banner (+20% damage aura).
- Maximal only: Mortar (arcing shots across most of the field), Flak (anti-air), Laser (continuous beam with ramping damage) and Gold Bank (income per wave).
- Runts, sprinters, swarms and tanks form the base; armored, regenerating and splitting enemies join later.
- Maximal only: flyers take the direct air route (only Sniper/Tesla/Flak/Laser hit them), cloaked enemies are visible only near Frost, Banner or Sniper towers, healers patch up their neighbours.
- Every 8th wave a boss marches in: lots of health, 5 lives lost on breakthrough, big reward.
- Classic = the main mode with 7 towers. Compact = 4 towers, 2 levels, more starting gold - the quick start. Maximal = 11 towers, A/B branches, special enemies and active abilities.
- Meadow (free), Canyon (from wave 5), Crossroads (from 10, the path crosses itself - strong for towers, but enemies are tougher) and Gauntlet (from 15, you may only build right next to the path).
Points come from every kill plus a wave bonus that grows with wave number and map difficulty. The milestone sits at 10,000 points - roughly wave 18-20 on Meadow.

Minigolf across 360 holes: 18 hand-built and 342 generated. The Classic and Pro courses ease you in with nine built holes each, the Tour offers 38 courses of nine generated holes with rising difficulty, and Random draws nine holes from everything and mirrors them at random.

Tour holes come from a seed: course 7, hole 3 looks the same on every start - nothing has to be stored for that. The arrows beside the course number page through the 38 courses, with the total par next to them.

The goal is to sink the ball in as few strokes as possible. By default a hole is picked up after eight strokes and scored at the minimum - if you would rather keep putting until the ball drops, switch the pick-up off in the setup screen (or with [P]).
The auto-aim can be switched off just as easily: normally the putter points at the cup before every stroke - without it you aim every hole entirely yourself.
In two-player mode each player takes the same hole one after the other; the scorecard on the right shows par and both results.

At the end of a round the Next button takes you straight to the following course (Classic -> Pro -> Tour 1 -> Tour 2 ...), so the same set of nine holes never repeats. Again replays the same course, Setup returns to the selection.
- Move the mouse to aim. Hold the left mouse button to load power, release to putt.

- Hold the right mouse button to lock the power: the bar freezes, turns gold and shows the percentage - so you can wait for the gap in the windmill with the shot fully charged. Releasing charges on; a locked power even survives the stroke, so the next left click putts with exactly that value.
- Left/right arrows aim, up/down set the power, [Space] putts.
- [G] toggles the aim line - you can also switch it off for good in the setup screen.

- [Z] toggles the auto-aim: on (default) the putter turns towards the cup before every stroke, off it keeps the direction you last picked - then you aim entirely yourself. On the tee of a new hole it points neutrally up the course.
- [R] cancels a charged shot: you may keep the mouse button held, the ball stays put and the stroke does not count - after releasing you simply charge again. [P] toggles the pick-up.
- [F] resets the current hole: strokes back to 0, ball back on the tee - same hole, same course. Holes you already finished stay on the scorecard.
- Sand slows the ball down hard, ramps accelerate in the direction of the arrows.
- Water costs a penalty stroke; the ball returns to its last safe spot.
- Rubber bumpers give speed back; windmills and moving blocks are all about timing. The power lock on the right mouse button keeps the shot charged until the gap lines up.
- Pipe: the ball disappears into one mouth and comes out of the other - direction and speed are kept.
- Ice lets the ball run almost forever, a sticky patch stops it dead.
- Boosters give a fixed shove when crossed, magnets pull the ball in or push it away.
- A one-way gate only lets you through in the arrow's direction; from the other side it is a wall.
- The turntable takes the ball along and carries it outwards, the jump ramp sends it flying over obstacles.
These eight obstacles come on top of the classic ones and can be placed freely in the hole editor - see the page "Custom holes".
Every hole is worth 600 points plus 300 for each stroke under par (and 300 less for each stroke over, never below 100).
A hole in one adds 500 points. The sum of all holes is your high score; the lowest stroke count per course is stored on top of that.
On the minigolf setup screen the MAPS tab leads to your own collection. "New" opens the hole editor, "Edit" picks up an existing hole again.
Every hole needs a name and an id. The id is the key: lower case, no spaces, only a-z, 0-9, - and _. It is also the file name suggested when you share the hole.

The hole sits on the left, the palette with four tools and fifteen obstacle types on the right. Rectangles are dragged out, round things take a single click, a pipe needs two clicks - entrance first, then exit.
With the select tool a click picks an object, dragging moves it, [Del] removes it. The values of the selected object then appear at the bottom: width, height, radius, direction, speed and so on.
At the top you set par as well as the width and height of the hole - from 60x80 up to 160x240 units. Anything that would stick out when you shrink it moves back in automatically.
[G] toggles the grid snap, [U] undoes, [Y] redoes, [S] saves and [Enter] tries the hole out right away. [Esc] goes back - with unsaved changes only after a confirmation.
"Template" replaces the current hole with one of twelve ready-made ones: Empty, Pipe, Island, Windmill, Zigzag, Water, Bumpers, Ramp, Ice, Maze, Magnet and Jump.
Every template always leaves a normal route open next to its trick - a hole that can only be solved with a trick would not be a template but a trap. All twelve are provably playable within par.
A template is a starting point, not a finished result: add your own obstacles, move the tee and the cup, change the size.
In the MAPS tab "Play" starts exactly the selected hole - with its own best score per hole.
In the PLAY tab there is a fifth course option, "Custom": that runs your whole collection one after another as a round, up to nine holes.
Everything is stored in ugc.json next to the game (next to the .exe for the built version) - the same place as mem.json and replay.json.
"Share" first asks for your name as the creator and for the file name; that one is already filled in with the id of the hole.
"Export as" opens the usual save dialog, "To Downloads" drops the file straight into the Downloads folder and tells you the path. Exactly one hole is exported each time.
The file carries the extension .lamapgzmap and contains JSON - you can send it like any other file. "Import" reads it back in; .json files are accepted on import as well.
If the id is already taken, the import automatically appends -2, -3 and so on instead of overwriting your existing hole.

Hole name, id and creator name all run through a word filter when saving, exporting AND importing, and it checks all 14 languages. Offensive text is rejected - no matter which language is currently set.

A pinball machine with three tables: Classic with three pop bumpers and one drop target bank, Space with four bumpers in a diamond and two banks, Lama with an open playfield and six targets in an arc.
Each game gives you 3 or 5 balls. After the launch a six second ball save runs: lose the ball in that window and it comes straight back to the shooter lane.
In two-player mode both players alternate ball by ball; the scores sit below each other in the info column.
- Hold the action key ([Space] by default) to load the plunger, release to launch. Pulled too softly? The ball rolls back and you may shoot again.
- Left/right (plus left/right [Shift]) work the flippers. With the mouse: left half of the screen = left flipper, right half = right flipper.
- The up key nudges the table. Three nudges in quick succession trigger TILT - the flippers stay dead until the ball drains.
Pop bumpers score 100, slingshots 50 and drop targets 250 - all times the current multiplier (up to x5).
Clearing a full target bank or collecting all four L-A-M-A lanes raises the multiplier by one.
Three balls locked in the saucer start multiball: three balls at once, and the bumpers pay a 2,500 point jackpot.
The info column on the right shows the multiplier, locked balls, cleared banks and the remaining ball save time.
A nudge saves a ball that is about to drain - but use it sparingly: the counter only resets after four quiet seconds.
The best result is stored per table, and the score of a game counts as your high score.
Ten frames by the official rules: two rolls per frame, strikes and spares earn bonus points, and the tenth frame grants bonus balls. The maximum is a 300 game.
The scorecard right below the header shows all ten frames with their rolls (X, /, -) and the running total.
In two-player mode both players alternate frame by frame.
1. Position on the foul line, 2. aiming angle, 3. spin (hook left or right), 4. power.
Every slider swings on its own; the action key or a click locks it in.
Left/right let you set a slider by hand instead - the swinging stops as soon as you do.
The lane is oiled up front: the hook only bites in the last third and then pulls the ball into the pocket between pins 1 and 3.
Leave the lane sideways and the ball drops into the gutter - that roll counts zero.
On Pro the sliders swing faster and the lane scatters a little more; on Easy everything is calmer. [G] toggles the guide line.
The ten pins are circles with real mass: the ball hits them, they knock each other over. A strike is the result of physics, not of luck.
The game total is your high score; the best result per difficulty is stored as well.
Hop cell by cell with the arrow keys or [W] [A] [S] [D]. [Space], [Enter] or a mouse click hop forward.
- Press the next direction while still in the air and you hop again right after landing. Holding a key does not keep hopping.
After the game over: [Enter] = again, [F] = characters, [S] = setup.
The route is generated endlessly row by row - there is always a walkable path.
- Grass: safe, but trees and rocks block the way.
- Roads: cars and trucks flatten you. The further you get, the faster and denser the traffic.
- Rivers: you can only stand on logs and lily pads. Logs carry you along - drift off the edge of the screen and you are out.
- Tracks: when the red warning light flashes and the bell rings, a train rushes in about a second later. Further on, whole stations with up to 5 tracks in a row await.
The camera slowly creeps forward. Dawdle too long or go back more than three rows and the eagle snatches you - a red edge at the bottom of the screen warns you first.
Score = furthest row reached. In Endless mode this is your high score (milestone: 150 rows).
From row 50 on, day and night alternate: at night headlights, trains and coins light up.
Coins are scattered along the route, the giant coin is worth 5. Collected coins are saved permanently.
In the CHARACTERS tab you spend them on new characters: frog, pig, penguin, cat, fox, llama, robot, ghost and unicorn (25 to 250 coins). The chicken is yours from the start.
- Achievements: "New Look" for your first purchased character, "Track Jumper" for 5 tracks in a row.
- Endless: a new route every run, counts for the high score.
- Daily Route: the same for everyone today (web version included), with its own daily best - does not count for the high score.
In the setup you toggle shadows [H] and the day/night cycle [N]; Left/Right switches between your characters.
The daily tracks of the last 30 days and every day you have already played can be replayed - with a separate best score per day.
- In the daily track setup, the arrows next to the date or [Page up]/[Page down] change the day; [K] or Archive opens the calendar.
- A past day uses the same seed as back then - the track is exactly the same.

Your icon races to the right on its own - all you decide is when to jump or fly. Hit a spike, fall into a pit or crash head-on into a block: boom, and a moment later the next attempt is already running.

A level is complete once you reach the finish. The bar at the top shows your progress in percent, the top right corner shows the coins of this attempt, and the attempt counter floats in the level at the start.
Every level has its own soundtrack; background, ground and orbs pulse to the beat. Music, progress bar and automatic checkpoints are toggled on the level select screen below the level card.
- [Space], [Up], [W], [Enter] or the left mouse button: jump or fly. Holding counts as pressing continuously - the cube then jumps again right after every landing.
- [R] restarts instantly, [Q] or [Backspace] returns to the level select, [Esc] pauses.
- [P] toggles practice mode; there [Z] places a checkpoint and [X] removes the last one.

- Level select: [Left]/[Right] browse, [1] to [9] and [0] jump straight to levels 1 to 10, [Home]/[End] to the first or last one, [Enter] starts, [P] picks Normal or Practice, [M] toggles the music, [Tab] cycles PLAY, MORE and LEVELS.
