Every press gets a timestamp and takes effect in exactly the physics step (1/240 second) in which it happened - so your jump lands right even when the computer stutters for a moment.
Portals transform your icon - every form flies differently:
- Cube: press = jump. It lands on blocks; crash into their side and the attempt is over.
- Ship: hold = rise, release = sink.
- Ball: a tap on the ground flips gravity - it then keeps rolling along the ceiling.
- UFO: every tap is a small flap, even in mid-air.
- Wave: hold = diagonally up, release = diagonally down. It is tiny, but any contact with a block shatters it.
Ship, ball, UFO and wave fly in a corridor between ground and ceiling - the portal decides how high it is.
- Pads sit on the ground and trigger on contact: yellow = high jump, pink = small jump, blue = flip gravity.
- Orbs float in the air and only trigger when you press while touching them - with the same colors. A short buffer forgives pressing a tick too early.
- Gravity portals: yellow turns the world upside down, blue turns it back. Speed portals switch to 0.5x, 1x, 2x or 3x.
- On top of that there are half blocks, small spikes, pits without ground and color triggers that recolor background and ground.
- Lama Launch, Neon Steps and Pixel Sprint (Easy, 1-2 stars): jumps, pads, orbs and the first ship.
- Orbit Garden and Moss Temple (Normal, 3 stars each): orb chains and calm stretches upside down on the ceiling.
- Gravity Tide, Magnet Fields, Skyline Rush and Hangar Run (Hard, 4-5 stars): gravity portals, ball, UFO and tight ship gates at double speed.
- Crystal Caves, Strobe City and Frost Relay (Harder, 6-7 stars): all five forms, rhythm passages and plenty of colour changes.
- Wave Reactor and Turbine Core (Insane, 9 stars each): the wave in a narrow tunnel.
- Lama Inferno and Lama Eclipse (Demon, 10 stars each): triple speed and everything at once.
Every level is provably beatable, including all three coins: while building them a solver beat each one with the real game code - and its solution even works when shifted by 1/240 second.
The MORE tab is a library of 80 extra levels in ten categories: starter, rhythm, coins, ship, UFO, ball, gravity, speed, wave and demon.
Pick a category at the top and search by name below it. Every row shows difficulty, length, the coins you found and your best run; "Random" throws one of the current selection at you.
These levels are solver-proven too - the goal and all three coins are reachable. They keep their own progress, but hand out no stars and no achievements: those stay with the campaign.
"As template" copies the chosen level into your own levels, where you can rebuild it. More on the page "Custom levels (Geometry Dash)".
In practice mode a crash sends you back to the last checkpoint instead of the start - green diamonds mark the checkpoints in the level, and the music simply keeps playing.
Automatic checkpoints appear about every two seconds (can be switched off), [Z] places your own and [X] removes the last one.
Practice has its own best score and earns neither stars nor coins.

Beat a level in normal mode and you earn its stars. Each level also hides three secret coins, often off the easiest path. They count once you finish the level with them - and each one is worth another star.
Your high score is your total number of stars (135 at most), and it can only grow. For every level the game remembers the best percentage in Normal and Practice, the coins found and the attempts.
- Achievements: "On the Beat" for your first completed level, "Coin Hunter" for all three coins of a level, "Demon Slayer" for Lama Inferno - plus a milestone at 20 stars.
In the LEVELS tab you build, play and share your own levels - see the page "Custom levels (Geometry Dash)".
The LEVELS tab on the Geometry Dash level select holds your own collection (up to 60 levels). "New" asks for a template first, "Edit" picks up an existing level again.

The canvas with its grid sits on the left, the palette on the right: Select and Eraser at the top, below them six groups - Blocks, Hazards, Pads & orbs, Portals, Speed and Extras (secret coins, color trigger). [1] to [6] pick the groups directly.
- Clicking or dragging places the chosen object, [R] rotates it: spikes and half blocks in four directions, pads up or down.
- With Select, dragging moves an object and [Del] removes it. A right-click always erases; right-dragging, the mouse wheel, the arrow keys or [A]/[D] scroll.
- The values of the selected object appear at the bottom: the corridor height for form portals, and target (background or ground), color and fade duration for the color trigger.
- The strip at the very bottom shows the whole level at a glance - a click jumps to that spot.
[U] undoes, [Y] redoes, [G] shows or hides the grid, [S] saves. [Esc] goes back - with unsaved changes only after a confirmation.
At most three coins per level. The finish is placed automatically a little behind the last object.
Every new level starts from a template: "Empty" begins from scratch, the other eleven bring a ready-made frame - starter, jumps, pads & orbs, ship, wave, ball, UFO, gravity, speed, coins and demon.
A template brings its objects, colours, music and start speed along. Because a solver played every template through, the copy carries the green check right away - until you change something.
Finished levels can be copied as well: in the MORE tab, "As template" adds the chosen level to your own, objects, colours and music included.
A copy is an ordinary level of your own: rebuild it, test it, save it, play it and share it.
The gear opens the level settings: start speed (0.5x to 3x), start mode, music style (Driving, Chiptune, Dreamy, Dark or no music), tempo in BPM plus background and ground color.
Name and id sit in the header at the top. The id is the key: lower case, no spaces, only a-z, 0-9, - and _ - and also the file name suggested when you share the level.
"Test" ([Enter]) plays the level from the start, "From here" ([T]) from the current spot - portals before it count as passed. [Esc] takes you back to the canvas.

Beat your level in a test from the very start and without practice mode, and it earns the green "verified" check mark. Any later change to objects, start speed or start mode removes it again - colors, name and music do not.
In the LEVELS tab "Play" starts the selected level normally, with its own best score and attempt counter.
"Share" asks for your name as the creator and for the file name. "Export as" opens the save dialog, "To Downloads" drops the file straight into the Downloads folder.

The file has the extension .lamapgzlevel and contains JSON. "Import" reads it back in (.json works too); if the id is already taken, -2, -3 ... is appended automatically. The verified check mark travels along.
Name, id and creator run through the word filter of all 14 languages when saving, exporting AND importing.
Everything is stored in ugc.json next to the game - the same file as your custom minigolf holes. In the browser version the levels stay in the browser's storage, and sharing downloads the file.
Two fleets, each on its own 10x10 sea: carrier (5 squares), battleship (4), cruiser (3), submarine (3) and destroyer (2). Players take turns firing at a square on the opponent's board.

On the left is the large target board with the radar, on the right your own waters and the fleet overview of both sides. A white ring means a miss, flames mean a hit. Once every square of a ship is hit, it sinks and its outline is revealed.
Whoever sinks all five enemy ships first wins. The summary then shows shots, hits, accuracy, turns and ships left for both sides.
- Drag ships from the dock on the right onto the board with the mouse - or click one, move it and click again. Placed ships can be moved the same way.
- [R] or a right-click rotates the held ship (or the ship under the mouse).
- The preview glows green when the position is allowed and red when it is not.
- Keyboard: the arrows move the frame, [Space] picks a ship up and puts it down, [Enter] takes the next missing ship.
- [X] deploys at random, [C] removes all ships. With a full fleet, [Enter] or "Ready!" starts the battle.
Your last layout is suggested again in the next round.
All three switches are saved instantly and apply to both sides:
- Ships may touch: OFF requires at least one free square around every ship, diagonals included. The blocked zone is highlighted while deploying.
- Salvo: each turn you get as many shots as you have ships afloat - lose ships and you fire fewer.
- Fire again after a hit: every hit gives the shot back, so you keep firing as long as you hit.
- Mouse: click a square on the target board.
- Keyboard: the arrows or your movement keys aim, [Space] or [Enter] fires.
- After a round: [Enter] = new round, [S] = back to setup. [Esc] pauses.
- Easy fires at random and only sometimes follows up on a hit.
- Medium searches at random, probes the neighbouring squares after a hit and extends lines of hits to the end of the ship.

- Hard works out for every square how many still-possible positions of the remaining ships would cover it (honouring the touch rule) and fires at the most likely one. While searching it uses a checkerboard pattern matched to the smallest remaining ship.
On average the AI needs about 70 (Easy), 60 (Medium) and 45 shots (Hard) to sink a whole fleet - and it only knows what you can see too.
In multiplayer you take turns at the same computer. Before deploying and before every turn a handover screen hides both fleets until the next player confirms with [Enter] or a click.
It also reports how many shots and hits the last attack on your fleet had. The web version only plays against the AI.
Every win against the AI counts one point; the high score is the most wins in one session. Two-player mode is not scored.
- Flawless Fleet: beat the AI without losing a single ship.
- Fleet Admiral: sink the hard AI's fleet.
- Spread your ships across the whole board and don't line them all up along the edge.
- When searching, every second square is enough (checkerboard) - once only long ships are left, even every third.
- Without the touch rule, every square around a sunk ship is guaranteed to be water.

Casino, Blackjack, Poker, Lama Crossing, Lama Mines, Lama Plinko and Lama Crash share one account: the llama chips (start 1000). Bets are taken immediately, wins are credited - everything is saved permanently.
Every game keeps its own balance. The Casino highscore is the peak of 1000 + casino balance; wins at Blackjack or Poker don't count here.
Broke (less than the minimum bet) means a bank loan: your account is filled back up to 1000. Loans don't count towards any balance; their number is shown top right.
European wheel with 37 pockets (0 to 36). Pick the chip value at the bottom: 1, 5, 25, 100 or 500 (keys [1] to [5] or mouse wheel).
Left click places a chip, right click takes it away again. Where you click decides the bet:
- Centre of a number: straight up, pays 35:1
- Edge between two numbers: split, 17:1
- Outer line of a number column: street with 3 numbers, 11:1 (next to zero also 0-1-2 and 0-2-3)
- Corner between four numbers: corner, 8:1 (outside at zero: 0-1-2-3)
- Corner on the outer line between two columns: six line, 5:1
- Column (2:1) and dozen (2:1), red/black, even/odd and low 1-18 / high 19-36 (each 1:1)
Next to the wheel you can see which bet is under the mouse and what it pays.
[Enter] or SPIN starts the round: the stake is taken and the winning number is drawn. The ball spirals in and drops exactly into that pocket - [Space] or a click fast-forwards.
Rebet [R] places the last round's bets again, Double [D] doubles all bets, Clear [Backspace] empties the table.
The last 12 numbers are shown at the top; winning bets show their payout.
5 reels, 3 rows, 10 paylines. Lines pay from 3 matching symbols from left to right; the numbers at the sides show where each line runs (hover = show line).
Bet per line: 1, 2, 5 or 10 ([+]/[-] or mouse wheel) - all 10 lines are always played.
- Llama = wild: replaces every symbol except the gold coin. 5 llamas on one line are the Llama Jackpot.
- Gold coin = scatter: 3, 4 or 5 coins anywhere pay 2, 10 or 50 times the total bet and award 10 free spins in which all wins count double. Free spins can be retriggered.
The paytable shows every payout for your current bet. The return to player is 96.1% - calculated exactly from the reel strips.
[Space], [Enter] or a click on the reels spins; pressing again during a spin fast-forwards.
Auto spin: [A] starts 10 rounds, [Shift]+[A] 25 rounds (or use the Auto button), press again to stop. [T] toggles turbo, [I] opens the paytable.
Won free spins are saved immediately and continue the next time you play.
- Casino milestone: highscore 5000
- Bullseye: win with a straight-up bet in roulette
- Llama Jackpot: 5 llamas on one payline
The llama crosses a road, a rope bridge, a river or a frozen lake lane by lane. Every lane you make raises the multiplier - if the llama gets caught, the bet is gone.
Pick a bet (10, 20, 50, 100, 200, 500, 1000, 2500, 5000 or 10000 llama chips) and press GO: the bet is taken and the llama steps into the first lane.

After every lane you make you decide: risk the NEXT lane or CASH OUT - then you get your bet times the current multiplier (rounded down to whole chips). Reaching the other side cashes out automatically, with confetti.
The top right shows the history of the last 12 rounds.

Every world has something coming that you have to time: on the road cars and trucks drive down every lane, on the rope bridge boulders crash through the bridge, on the river driftwood floats towards you and on the ice lake ice blocks slide your way.
If you press GO or NEXT while an obstacle is in the next lane, the llama gets run over or hit and lies flat - the bet is lost. So wait for a gap.

The lane the llama is standing in is protected: on the road a barrier drops and the cars stop in front of the llama, in the other worlds obstacles in your lane vanish. So you can wait calmly for the right gap.
The higher the difficulty, the denser and faster the traffic.

On top of that every lane carries a random risk that even perfect timing can't prevent: on the road a speeder suddenly appears, on the bridge the plank breaks, on the river the stone slips away and on the ice lake the ice breaks.
Four levels - chosen before each round with the buttons in the bottom bar or with [1] to [4]:
- Easy: 22 lanes, risk 1/12 per lane (about 8%), up to ×6.57
- Medium: 20 lanes, risk 1/6 (about 17%), up to ×37.18
- Hard: 18 lanes, risk 3/10 (30%), up to ×595.67
- Extreme: 15 lanes, risk 1/2 (50%), up to ×31,784.96 - every lane doubles the multiplier: ×1.94, ×3.88, ×7.76 …

The multipliers are fixed tables, calculated so that with clean timing every strategy returns about 97% of the stake in the long run - no matter at which lane you cash out. The house edge is therefore about 3%.
Switch with the four world buttons top left or with [W]; the world doesn't change the odds:
- Road (default): a street seen from above, with sidewalks. The llama crosses lane by lane over zebra-crossing pieces while cars and trucks drive past - and now and then a speeder.
- Rope bridge: planks over a canyon, boulders crash down - if the plank breaks, the llama falls.
- River: stepping stones in the water, driftwood floats towards you - if the stone slips away, splash.
- Ice lake: ice floes on the frozen lake, ice blocks slide towards you - cracks spread, then the floe breaks.
In every world the llama wears a scarf in the game's accent colour.
- [Space], [Right] or a click on the next lane: GO or NEXT - best when the lane is clear
- [Enter] or [C]: cash out (before a round, [Enter] works like GO)
- [Up] / [Down], [+] / [-] or mouse wheel: change the bet
- [1] to [4]: difficulty, [W]: switch world (road, rope bridge, river, ice lake)
Bet, difficulty and world can only be changed between rounds. World, difficulty and your last bet are saved in settings.json (section lamacrossing).
Lama Crossing plays with the shared Llama Bank account - together with Blackjack, Poker, Casino, Lama Mines, Lama Plinko and Lama Crash (start 1000, stored in mem.json).
The highscore is the peak of 1000 + your Lama Crossing balance; wins at Blackjack, Poker or the Casino don't count here.
Below 10 chips you are broke: [Enter] or a click takes a bank loan and fills your account back up to 1000. Loans don't count towards the balance.
Stopping mid-crossing is safe: bet, difficulty and lane are saved, and the next start continues exactly there.
- Lama Crossing regular: 25 rounds
- Milestone: highscore 3000
- Lama Crossing master: highscore 10000
- Other Side (rare): Get the llama all the way across in Lama Crossing
- Nerves of Steel (epic): Cash out at ×10 or more in Lama Crossing
- Tightrope Walk (legendary): Cash out at ×100 or more on Extreme in Lama Crossing
- No need to rush: the llama is safe in its own lane. Keep an eye on the next lane and only go when a real gap comes.
- Every lane is drawn afresh - a run of losses says nothing about the next lane.
- With clean timing you get all the way across in about every 7th round on Easy, every 38th on Medium, every 614th on Hard and only one in 32,768 on Extreme.

- For Nerves of Steel (×10), 4 lanes are enough on Extreme (×15.52), 7 on Hard (×11.77) and 13 on Medium (×10.37); on Easy it never happens (at most ×6.57). Tightrope Walk (×100 on Extreme) takes 7 lanes (×124.16) - that works out in about every 128th round.
- Decide beforehand at which multiplier you will cash out - and stick to it. Thanks to the fixed return no strategy is better than another, only more or less risky.
Under every hidden tile lies a gem or a mine. Every gem you find raises the multiplier - a mine costs you the bet.

Pick a bet (10, 20, 50, 100, 200, 500, 1000, 2500, 5000 or 10000 llama chips) and press PLAY: the bet is taken and the field is drawn. From now on it is fixed where the mines are - verifiable with the fairness check.

Then you reveal tile after tile: with a click, with the arrow keys and [Space], or with [R] or the Random tile button on a random hidden tile. From the first gem on you can CASH OUT at any time - then you get your bet times the current multiplier.

Once all gems are found, the round cashes out automatically: ALL MINE! Hit a mine and it explodes, the screen shakes and the bet is gone. Either way - also after cashing out - the remaining tiles are revealed, dimmed, so you can see where the mines were. The field stays like that until you play on or change a setting.
The top right shows the history of the last 12 rounds - the newest on the right, a mine as a red ×0.
Four field sizes - chosen before each round with the buttons or with [1] to [4]: 4×4 (16 tiles), 5×5 (25 tiles, default), 6×6 (36 tiles) and 7×7 (49 tiles).

Set the number of mines with [Left] / [Right], the arrow buttons or the six quick-pick buttons: from 1 up to the number of tiles minus 1 - at least one gem always remains. The default is 3 mines. The quick picks per field size are:
More mines means: every gem is worth more, but the next tile is safe less often. With 24 mines on 5×5 the very first gem pays ×24.25 - at a 4% chance.
Field size, mines and bet can only be changed between rounds.
The multiplier only depends on how many gems you have found so far - not on which tiles they were. It exactly balances the chance of getting that far, minus 3% for the bank:
- multiplier = 0.97 divided by the chance of finding k gems in a row
- that chance is a product with one factor per gem: gems/tiles × (gems - 1)/(tiles - 1) × …

- as a short formula: 0.97 × C(N, M) / C(N - k, M), rounded down to hundredths. Here N is the number of tiles, M the number of mines, k the number of gems found and C(n, m) the binomial coefficient “n choose m”.
Example 5×5 with 3 mines: the first tile is safe with 22 out of 25 (88%), so it pays 0.97 / 0.88 = ×1.10. After two gems the chance is 22/25 × 21/24 = 77% - that makes ×1.25.

It goes on with ×1.44, ×1.67 and ×1.95 after 5 gems, ×4.90 after 10, ×10.14 after 13, ×18.59 after 15, ×111.55 after 19 and ×557.75 after 21. Find all 22 gems and you get ×2,231 - that happens in one round out of 2300.

Floor: every gem raises the multiplier by at least 0.01 - so even the first one pays at least ×1.01. The plain formula would give only ×0.99 on 6×6 with 1 mine, for example. Only three steps are lifted: the first gem on 6×6 with 1 mine and the first two on 7×7 with 1 mine.

The maximum win is ×100,000. If the multiplier reaches this limit, the round cashes out automatically right away: MAX WIN! When clearing the whole field this already happens from 5×5 with 6 mines, 6×6 with 5 and 7×7 with 4 mines; never on 4×4. There is no more, even if the formula would give more.

Because chance and multiplier balance each other, every strategy returns about 97% of the stake in the long run - no matter which field size, how many mines and after how many gems you cash out. Rounding down makes it 96 to 97% depending on the step. The three lifted steps are slightly above (at most 98.94% for the first gem on 7×7 with 1 mine), the capped step clearly below. The house edge is therefore about 3%.

Fractions are not lost: whole chips are paid out, the rest in hundredths is remembered and added to your next payout. So 10 chips × 1.01 first pays 10 chips, the remaining 0.10 comes later - this way small bets get the full return too.

Before a round the header shows the top multiplier of your setting (all gems found) and the number of gems and mines. During a round you see everything you need for your next decision next to the field:
- the current multiplier and your win if you cash out now
- the multiplier after the next gem and the win on the next tile
- the chance that the next tile is safe: remaining gems divided by remaining hidden tiles - 88% on the first click on 5×5 with 3 mines, a little less with every gem after that
- how many gems you have found and a bar with the next 5 steps: how many gems pay which multiplier

The mascot llama with a miner's helmet and headlamp is right there with you: it cheers at every gem while the mine cart next to it fills up, and at a mine it gets a fright and ends up covered in soot. From ×3 coins rain down, from ×10 and when clearing the field there is confetti too.

[A] or the Auto button opens auto mode between rounds. The window sits over the side panel and leaves the grid free: with a click or with the arrow keys and [Space] you mark the tiles that will be revealed every round - at most as many as there are gems. The game remembers your choice per field size; [Del], [Backspace] or Clear removes all marks.

The window shows how many tiles are marked and what the round pays if all of them are safe: multiplier and chance. You also choose the number of rounds (5, 10, 25, 50 or 100) and, if you like, two limits: stop at a profit of and stop at a loss of (off, 100, 500, 1000, 5000, 10000 or 50000 chips, counted from the start).

START AUTO or [Enter]: every round takes the bet and quickly reveals the marked tiles one after another. If all of them are safe, it cashes out - with the multiplier for as many gems as you marked. If a mine is under one of the marked tiles, the round is lost.

Auto mode runs until all rounds are played, a limit kicks in, your chips don't cover the next bet or you press STOP, [Space], [Enter], [A] or [Esc]. If you stop in the middle of a round, it stays open - you reveal more by hand or cash out. Bet, field size and mines are locked while auto mode runs.
[T] toggles turbo - also when playing by hand: flipping tiles, explosions and auto rounds run two and a half times as fast.
Lama Mines is provably fair: the minefield is fixed before you click the first tile - and after the round you can check that nothing was moved. Four values make this work:
- Server seed: a secret random value (32 characters) that the game fixes before the round.

- Hash: the SHA-256 fingerprint of the server seed. It is shown before the round (hash of the next round). The seed can't be worked out from it - but even one different character in the seed would give a completely different hash.
- Client seed: your share of the randomness (8 characters). New client seed rolls a fresh one - only outside a round. So the game doesn't decide the result on its own.
- No.: the round number. It goes up by one every round, so no two rounds are alike.

Game name, server seed, client seed and round number make up the randomness of the round (mulberry32). It shuffles the list of all tiles (counted row by row, starting top left), and the first places of the shuffled list - as many as there are mines - become mines.
After the round the server seed is revealed; by then the hash of the next round is already fixed.

[F] opens the Fairness window: at the top the hash of the next round (during a round also the hash of this round), your client seed and the round number, below that the last 12 rounds with No., hash and result, newest at the top (the mouse wheel scrolls). Clicking a row shows field size, mines, hash, server seed and client seed.

Verify computes the SHA-256 of the seed again, compares it with the hash shown beforehand, rebuilds the minefield and also checks the result - were the revealed tiles right, does the multiplier match? A tick or cross and a small preview of the field show: Matches or Does not match.
You can also check the hash yourself: compute the SHA-256 of the server seed with any tool and compare it with the hash.

[S] opens the statistics of your profile: rounds, won and lost, your return (what percentage of your bets came back), wagered and paid out, net result, biggest win and best multiplier - plus gems found, mines hit and fields cleared.
A curve shows the net result of the last 100 rounds. A round counts as won if more was paid out than wagered.
In the long run your return settles at about 97% - over a few rounds it can swing a lot up or down.
- Before a round: [Space] or [Enter] = PLAY, [1] to [4] = field size, [Left] / [Right] = number of mines
- [Up] / [Down], [+] / [-] or mouse wheel: change the bet (only between rounds)
- During a round: clicking a tile reveals it. The arrow keys move a cursor; the first [Space] only shows it, every further one reveals the tile under it.
- [R] or the Random tile button: reveal a random hidden tile; [Enter], [C] or CASH OUT: cash out (from the first gem on)
- After the result: [Space] or PLAY starts the next round right away, other keys go back to the setup.
- [A]: auto mode, [S]: statistics, [F]: fairness, [T]: turbo - or the four buttons at the top. [Esc] or a click next to the window closes it, [Esc] also stops auto mode.

The keys are fixed and don't depend on your key bindings - player keys like WASD don't apply here. Field size, number of mines, your last bet, turbo and the auto settings are saved in settings.json (section lamamines).
Lama Mines plays with the shared Llama Bank account - together with Blackjack, Poker, Casino, Lama Crossing, Lama Plinko and Lama Crash (start 1000, stored in mem.json).
The highscore is the peak of 1000 + your Lama Mines balance; wins in the other Llama Bank games don't count here.
Below 10 chips you are broke: [Space], [Enter] or a click takes a bank loan and fills your account back up to 1000. Loans don't count towards the balance.

Stopping mid-round is safe: the bet is booked at the start, and after every gem found the field size, mines, the seeds of the round and the revealed tiles are saved. On the next start the field is recalculated from the seed and you continue exactly there.
History, fairness data, statistics, the auto marks and the carried-over fraction belong to your profile.
- Lama Mines regular: 25 rounds
- Milestone: highscore 3000
- Lama Mines master: highscore 10000
- Treasure Vault (rare): Clear a whole field in Lama Mines – every gem found
- Deep Digger (epic): Cash out at ×10 or more in Lama Mines
- Diamond Llama (legendary): Cash out at ×1000 or more in Lama Mines
- Every round is drawn afresh, and no tile is safer than another - not the corners, not the middle. Patterns from earlier rounds don't help.
- Treasure Vault: on 4×4 with 1 mine, clearing the field works in one round out of 16 (×15.52) - just like with 15 mines, where there is only one gem. On 5×5 with 3 mines it is only one in 2300.
- Deep Digger (×10): on 5×5 with 3 mines 13 gems are enough (×10.14), which works out in about every 10th to 11th round. With 24 mines the very first gem pays ×24.25 - in one round out of 25.

- Diamond Llama (×1000): the best routes work out in about one round out of 1100, for example 5×5 with 10 mines after 10 gems (×1,055.84) or 7×7 with 12 mines after 19 gems (×1,034.71). On 5×5 with 3 mines it only works by clearing the whole field (×2,231).
- In auto mode only the number of marked tiles counts, not which ones: 5 marked tiles on 5×5 with 3 mines are all safe in 49.6% of rounds and then pay ×1.95.

- Decide beforehand after how many gems you will cash out - and stick to it. Thanks to the fixed return no strategy is better than another, only more or less risky. Going for the maximum win doesn't pay: the capped step pays less than its risk would be worth.

A golden ball of yarn drops through a triangle of pegs. At every peg it bounces left or right and lands in one of the slots at the bottom. Every slot shows a multiplier: bet times multiplier is your payout.
Pick a bet per ball (1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 200, 500 or 1000 llama chips) and press DROP: the bet is taken, the llama at the top of the board nods and lets the ball drop.

The outer slots pay the most, the ones in the middle return less than the bet - but that's where most balls land. You get bet times multiplier in whole chips; whatever is left below one chip is remembered and added to the next ball.

The slot that was hit bounces, a popup shows the multiplier, and the higher it is, the brighter the sound. From ×10 coins rain down, from ×100 there's a banner and confetti as well. The top right shows the history of the last 12 balls.
You set both before dropping; while balls are on the board or auto mode is running, they are locked. The game also shows the highest multiplier and the exact return of the chosen table.
- Rows: 8 to 16 rows of pegs with [Left] / [Right] (default 12). With n rows there are n + 1 slots.
- Risk: Low, Medium (default) or High with [1] to [3].
More rows make the edge slots rarer and higher. The risk decides how far apart the middle and the edge are:
- Low: middle ×0.7, edge ×5.3 (8 rows) up to ×16 (16 rows) - small, frequent wins
- Medium: middle ×0.4–0.5, edge ×13 up to ×110
- High: middle ×0.2, edge ×32 up to ×1,000 - almost always less than your bet, very rarely a huge hit
With 16 rows, about 55% of all balls return less than the bet on Low, 79% on Medium and as many as 92% on High.

The board is a Galton board: at every peg the ball goes left or right with exactly 50% - like a coin toss. The slot is simply the number of bounces to the right: with 12 rows that's 0 (far left) to 12 (far right).

A ball only reaches the very edge if it bounces the same way at every single peg. Lots of paths lead to the middle, though. That's why the balls pile up in the middle in a bell curve (binomial distribution):
- 8 rows: middle slot 27.34%, each edge slot 1 in 256
- 12 rows: middle slot 22.56%, each edge slot 1 in 4,096
- 16 rows: middle slot 19.64%, each edge slot 1 in 65,536
Move the mouse over a slot: it shows its multiplier, its chance (even tiny ones like 0.0015%) and what it pays at your bet.

The 27 tables (9 row counts × 3 risks) are symmetric, never get smaller towards the edge and - calculated exactly - pay back 96.9% to 97.1% of all bets in the long run. The house edge is therefore about 3%, whatever you set. Rows and risk only change how wildly your luck swings.

You don't have to wait for a ball to land: up to 50 balls can bounce across the board at the same time - the "In play" counter keeps track. Hold [Space] and after a short moment they drop in rapid fire - so densely that about 30 balls are in play at once.

Each ball's path is drawn the moment it is dropped. That's why bet and payout are booked and saved together right away - but you only see the payout once the ball reaches the bottom. Only then can you bet those winnings again.
If you leave the game while balls are still falling, nothing is lost: the chips are already booked, and achievements from those balls are awarded when you leave.
Turbo halves the balls' flight time and the gap between rapid-fire drops - toggle it with [T].
[A] opens auto mode. There you set (the window also works out the total stake of the run):
- Stop at a profit of / Stop at a loss of: off, 100, 500, 1000, 5000, 10000 or 50000 chips
- Turbo on or off

START AUTO drops the balls one after another with your current bet, rows and risk; those three are locked meanwhile. Auto mode ends when all balls have been dropped, the profit or loss since the start reaches a limit, your chips no longer cover the next ball even after the flying balls have landed, or you press STOP, [Space] or [Esc]. Balls already on their way still land.
The auto settings are saved in settings.json (section lamaplinko).
In Lama Plinko you can check for yourself that no ball is steered after the fact ("provably fair"). Three values make that possible:
- Server seed: a secret random value of 32 characters that the game fixes before the drop. Every ball gets its own.

- Hash: the SHA-256 fingerprint of the server seed. You can see it before the drop. It doesn't give away the seed, but any other seed would have a completely different hash - so the game can no longer swap the seed.
- Client seed: your own share (8 characters). "New client seed" rolls a new one as soon as no ball is in the air - so the game doesn't decide the randomness on its own.

On top of that there is the number (nonce), which goes up by 1 with every ball. Server seed, client seed and number together make up the ball's randomness: one coin toss per row, and every "right" moves it one slot further to the right.
After the landing the server seed is revealed - by then the hash of the next ball is already fixed.

[F] opens the fairness window with the last 12 balls: number, hash, server seed and client seed, plus rows, risk, slot and multiplier. "Verify" computes the seed's SHA-256 again, compares it with the hash shown beforehand and recalculates the ball's path: "Matches" means everything checks out, "Does not match" would reveal a mismatch. A mini preview shows the recalculated path.

For the curious: the random generator is mulberry32, seeded with the FNV-1a value of the text "lamaplinko|server seed|client seed|number". Each row draws a number between 0 and 1; below 0.5 means right. So every ball can also be recalculated with your own tools.
[S] opens your profile's statistics for Lama Plinko:
- Tiles: Rounds, Won, Lost, Wagered, Paid out, Net result, Biggest win, Best multiplier, Your return. Every ball counts on its own; won means more than the bet came back, lost means less.
- a net-result curve of the last 100 balls
- the hit distribution: your hits per slot as bars, the expected distribution (binomial) in gold - separately for each row count, switch with [Left] / [Right]

At first your return jumps around a lot (one edge hit on High sends it way up); with many balls it approaches about 97%. In the same way, after a few hundred balls the bars close in on the golden curve.
- [Space], [Enter] or a click on DROP or the board: drop a ball - hold for rapid fire
- [Up] / [Down], [+] / [-] or mouse wheel: change the bet per ball
- [Left] / [Right]: rows (8 to 16), [1] to [3]: risk
- [A]: auto mode, [S]: statistics, [F]: fairness, [T]: turbo
- [Esc]: close an open window or stop auto mode
- Mouse over a slot: multiplier, chance and payout at your bet

In the windows: in the auto window [Up] / [Down] picks a line, [Left] / [Right] changes it and [Enter] or [Space] starts or stops. In the statistics [Left] / [Right] switches the row count of the distribution. In the fairness window the arrow keys or the mouse wheel pick a ball, [Enter] verifies it and [C] gets a new client seed. [Esc] or the same letter key closes the window again.
Everything also works with the mouse; clicking next to an open window closes it. Rows, risk, bet, turbo and the auto settings are saved in settings.json (section lamaplinko).
Lama Plinko plays with the shared Llama Bank account - together with Blackjack, Poker, Casino, Lama Crossing, Lama Mines and Lama Crash (start 1000, stored in mem.json).
The highscore is the peak of 1000 + your Lama Plinko balance; wins in the other games don't count here.

If your account doesn't cover the chosen bet, pick a smaller one. With 0 chips you are broke: [Enter] or a click takes a bank loan and fills your account back up to 1000. Loans don't count towards the balance.
History, statistics and fairness data belong to your profile and are stored in mem.json as well.
- Lama Plinko regular: 25 rounds
- Milestone: highscore 3000
- Lama Plinko master: highscore 10000
- Edge Hit (rare): Hit the outermost slot in Lama Plinko (12 rows or more)
- Yarn Storm (epic): Have 25 balls on the board at once in Lama Plinko
- Plinko Legend (legendary): Hit the outermost slot in Lama Plinko with 16 rows on high risk
- Every ball is independent: after ten hits in the middle the edge is not "due".
- No setting beats the return. On Low your account barely swings, on High you lose most of the time - with a small chance of a huge hit.

- Small bets are no disadvantage: fractions of a chip are never lost. On 1 chip, ×0.7 pays nothing at first, but the 0.7 chips are remembered and paid out with one of the next balls as soon as a whole chip is full. So the return of about 97% holds for every bet.
- Edge Hit: fastest with 12 rows - there about 1 in 2,048 balls lands on the very edge (left or right). At 1 chip per ball that costs only about 3 chips per 100 balls on average.

- Yarn Storm: just hold [Space] - rapid fire puts about 30 balls on the board at once with any number of rows, and after about 2 seconds the achievement is yours. Auto mode drops too leisurely for it.
- Plinko Legend: with 16 rows on High only 1 in 32,768 balls lands on the very edge - with auto runs of 1000 balls that takes about 33 runs on average. That slot pays ×1,000, though.
- Set a budget beforehand and use the loss limit in auto mode.

Your llama rides up in a balloon, and the multiplier grows with every second: ×1.00, ×1.50, ×2.00 … If you cash out, you get your bet times the multiplier at that moment. If the balloon pops first, the bet is gone.

Pick a bet (10, 20, 50 … up to 10000 llama chips) and press PLAY: the bet is taken, and after a short 3-2-1 the balloon lifts off. From ×1.01 on you can CASH OUT at any time - the llama jumps off with a parachute and the win is credited right away.
When the balloon pops is fixed before the start - but nobody can see it: neither the balloon nor the music or sounds give anything away. It simply keeps inflating the higher it goes.

After you cash out, the empty balloon flies on until it pops - so you can see how far it would have gone. [Space] or FAST FORWARD speeds this up. The top right shows the pop points of the last 12 rounds.
Timing: ×2 after 11.6 seconds, ×10 after 38 seconds, ×100 after 77 seconds, ×100,000 after 3.2 minutes. Turbo ([T]) makes everything three times as fast.

With [Z] or the switch on card 2 you take a second llama along: two bets in the same round, each with its own amount and its own auto target. Both fly in the same balloon - for example a careful one with a target of ×1.50 and a bold one with a target of ×10.
- [Space] / [Enter] / [C] or CASH OUT at the bottom: every bet still flying cashes out
- [1] / [2] or the button on the card: only that bet
- [H] or HALF: every bet that hasn't been split yet cashes out half, the other half keeps flying
- [Q] / [W] or the half button on the card: half of that bet only
Each bet can be halved once. The llama drops the cashed-out half as a money bag on a mini parachute.

Auto target: with [Left] / [Right] (or the mouse wheel over the target) you set the multiplier at which a bet cashes out by itself (×1.01 to ×100,000); [X] switches it on or off. If the balloon reaches the target, the payout is exactly at the target - even if it pops at that very moment.

sections.h: How the pop point is decided
body: For every round a random number r between 0 and 2^32 - 1 is drawn. The pop point is 97 × 2^32 / (2^32 - r), rounded down to hundredths, at least ×1.00 and at most ×100,000. About 4% of rounds pop right at ×1.00 - before anyone can cash out.
This leads to a simple rule: the chance of reaching a target x is 97% divided by x. No matter when you cash out - in the long run 97% of your bets come back:
If you cash out by hand at some multiplier, you win exactly when the balloon pops later - just as if you had set it as your auto target.
Reach ×100,000 and you land on the moon: maximum win, and every bet still flying is paid out at ×100,000.
Carry-over: whatever is left in hundredths when a payout is rounded down is added to the next one - so even small bets lose nothing.
The higher the multiplier, the higher the balloon flies - through six worlds:
- Llama meadow (from ×1): pasture, fence and barn stay behind below
- Sea of clouds (from ×1.50): clouds and flocks of birds
- Storm front (from ×3): rain, lightning and planes
- Northern lights (from ×10): stars and dancing auroras
- Outer space (from ×100): the curve of the Earth, satellites, shooting stars - and the moon keeps getting bigger
- Moon (×100,000): the moon landing
The suspense music gets faster and higher with every world; from ×2 the stretched balloon starts to creak. [M] switches the music on or off.
[A] opens auto mode (only between rounds). There you set:
- Stop at a profit of / Stop at a loss of: off, 100, 500, 1000, 5000, 10000 or 50000 chips
- Turbo on or off

START AUTO plays the rounds one after another with your bets and auto targets; a bet without an auto target gets one switched on. Once everyone is out, it fast-forwards automatically. You can still cash out by hand at any time.
Auto runs until the number of rounds is reached, a limit kicks in, your chips run short or you press STOP, [Esc] or [A] - a round already in flight then finishes normally.
In Lama Crash you can check for yourself that the pop point is not changed after the fact ("provably fair"):
- Server seed: a secret random value of 32 characters, fixed before the round
- Hash: the SHA-256 fingerprint of the server seed - visible before the start
- Client seed: your own share (8 characters); "New client seed" rolls a new one while no round is running
On top of that comes the round number (nonce). After the round the server seed is revealed - by then the hash of the next round is already fixed.
[F] shows the last 12 rounds. "Verify" ([Enter]) checks the hash, recalculates the pop point and shows with a tick or a cross whether everything matches - plus a mini curve with your cash-outs.
For the curious: the randomness is mulberry32, seeded with the FNV-1a value of "lamacrash|server seed|client seed|number"; r is its first number.
[S] opens your profile's statistics for Lama Crash:
- Tiles: Rounds, Won, Lost, Your return, Wagered, Paid out, Net result, Biggest win, Best multiplier (highest cash-out), Top pop point, Half cash-outs and Close calls
- a net-result curve of the last 100 rounds
- the distribution of your rounds' pop points as bars, the expected distribution in gold
- [Space] / [Enter] or PLAY: start a round; in flight: cash out all; afterwards: fast-forward
- [1] / [2] or [Tab]: select a card (before the round) or cash out a single bet (in flight)
- [Up] / [Down], [+] / [-] or mouse wheel: bet of the selected card
- [Left] / [Right] or mouse wheel over the target: auto target; [X]: auto target on/off; [Z]: second bet
- [H]: half of every unsplit bet; [Q] / [W]: half of bet 1 or 2
- [A]: auto mode, [S]: statistics, [F]: fairness, [T]: turbo, [M]: music
- [Esc]: close a window or stop auto, otherwise pause

The windows can only be opened while no bet is flying. If the game window loses focus while a bet is flying, the game pauses by itself. Bets, targets, turbo, music and the auto settings are saved in settings.json (section lamacrash).
Lama Crash plays with the shared Llama Bank account - together with Blackjack, Poker, Casino, Lama Crossing, Lama Mines and Lama Plinko (start 1000, stored in mem.json).

PLAY books the bet and saves the round in one go, and every cash-out credits the win immediately. If you leave the game mid-flight, nothing is lost: on the next start there is a countdown and the balloon climbs on from exactly where it was - after all, the pop point is already fixed.
The highscore is the peak of 1000 + your Lama Crash balance. Below 10 chips you are broke: [Enter] or a click takes a bank loan that tops your account back up to 1000.
- Lama Crash regular: 25 rounds
- Milestone: highscore 3000
- Lama Crash master: highscore 10000
- Close Call (rare): Cash out manually at ×2 or more - at most 5% before the pop
- Aurora Pilot (epic): Cash out at ×10 or more
- Space Llama (legendary): Cash out at ×1000 or more
- Every round is independent: after five early pops, a big flight is not "due".
- No strategy beats the 97%. Low targets win often and little, high ones rarely and a lot.
- Two bets mix both: one locks in a win early, the other flies far.
- Close Call only counts when you cash out by hand - auto targets don't count.
- Aurora Pilot: an auto target of ×10 hits about every tenth round; Space Llama with a target of ×1,000 about every thousandth - with turbo such a flight takes 38 seconds.
- Set a budget beforehand and use the loss limit in auto mode.
